Smidge gives Poppy a super lift, and Biggie cries happy tears when he gets his invitation. Poppy visits Creek, who gives good advice, and Diamond, who shakes glitter when he dances. Satin and Chanille will make dresses for Poppy, and Poppy practices dance moves with Cooper, who has four feet. DJ Suki makes a special playlist for the Afterparty, and Fuzzbert loves to tickle the trolls. Branch does not want to sing, dance, or hug, so everyone is shocked. Poppy gives Branch a special invitation and tells him he can find his true colors. Then Smidge sends glitter sparkles into the sky, DJ Suki turns up the volume, and all the trolls sing, dance, and hug at Poppy’s party.

summary_text: The narrator walks near a construction site and thinks about dinosaurs that lived there millions of years ago. Big machines like a backhoe make the narrator feel small, just like people would feel next to a Tyrannosaurus Rex. The narrator has been reading a book about digging up dinosaurs and sees dinosaur skeletons in a museum. There are Apatosaurus, Iguanodon, Triceratops, and Tyrannosaurus. The narrator learns that dinosaurs lived long ago, on every continent, and then died out 65 million years ago. For a long time, people did not know about them. Later, people found fossils in rock. The story explains that a dinosaur died, sank in a river, and slowly turned to stone under sand. Fossil hunters carefully dig bones from the ground, wrap them, study them, and make casts. Museums can now show copies of skeletons. The story ends by saying many animals today, like lizards, turtles, rhinos, hippos, and elephants, may be related to dinosaurs.

summary_text: Before spring comes, the trees look like black sticks in the sky. The grass is brown, and the garden is only dirt. The snow sits in little mounds, and if you wait, it gets smaller and smaller until it is gone. Then spring comes. Spring brings leaves and blossoms to the trees. It turns the grass green and adds little flowers. Seeds start growing, and an egg can become a bird. Spring also brings sun, rain, and more rain. There can be mud and puddles, so umbrellas may be needed. In the garden, green shoots push through the dirt. Spring calls out the willows and new kittens too. Spring may come quickly or slowly, and it changes a lot. When spring is finally here to stay, there are buds, bees, boots, bubbles, worms, wings, wind, and wheels. You can see, smell, and hear that spring is here. Then it is time to wait for summer.

summary_text: Po and Pcoo played with building blocks and worked well together. They built a big castle tower, but they needed one more block to finish it. Pcoo took a block from the bottom and put it on top. Then the tower fell down. Po got angry with Pcoo, and Pcoo blamed Po. Soon both friends were angry and did not want to talk or play. They stacked blocks and built a tall wall between them. Ellie came, but when she saw how stubborn they were, she left. Po and Pcoo played alone on their own sides of the wall, but it was not fun. Pcoo found a photo and felt sad because he missed Po. Po saw the picture too, and he felt sad as well. They both cried. Then Ellie came back and pushed the wall far away. Po and Pcoo saw each other again, ran to hug, and learned that making up is better than being angry. Hooray for friends!

summary_text: It is the first day of fall, and Pete the Cat feels blue because he likes summer better. Mom tells him to remember things he loves about autumn. Grandpa helps him knit a warm scarf, and Pete saves some yarn. Pete rides on a hay wagon with his family and packs hay. With Callie, he picks apples, eats apple donuts, and puts an apple in his backpack. Pete plays football, scores a touchdown, and takes Bob’s football. At home, he rakes and jumps in leaf piles, then collects leaves. His backpack bursts with souvenirs. Pete and Mom use them to decorate the Thanksgiving table. Family and friends come, eat, laugh, and tell stories. Pete discovers that he loves many autumn things, but most of all he loves his family and friends.

summary_text: Ordinary Mary picked blue berries from a vacant lot. She put them in a big brown bowl on Mrs. Bishop’s porch. Mrs. Bishop was happy and baked blueberry muffins. She gave plates to five people, including paper boy Billy Parker. Billy ate every crumb and then brought papers to people instead of throwing them in bushes. Each person passed kindness to five more people. Mr. Mori helped people with heavy bags. Mario helped Joseph, and Joseph gave Sahar a new bag. Sahar cheered Sophia, and Sophia called people to make them happy. Dr. Tom gave balloons to hospital patients. Peter helped Eric, and Eric invited his shy sister Dai to the park. Dai helped Louise, who gave food to Amara. Amara gave Kate a show ticket. Kate sent Mary a heart necklace. Mary’s one good deed traveled from person to person. In 16 days, love touched billions of people. The world changed because Ordinary Mary did one good deed. The story says one good deed can help make the world better.

summary_text: Leonardo was a monster, but he was not very scary. He was not big like Eleanor, did not have 1,642 teeth like Tony, and was not weird like Hector. Leonardo tried hard to scare people, but he could not do it. One day, he had an idea. He wanted to find the most scaredy-cat kid in the whole world and scare him. Leonardo looked and looked until he found Sam. He sneaked up on Sam and made loud monster sounds like "Grrr" and "Roar". Sam started to cry, and Leonardo thought he had done it. He shouted that he had scared the tuna salad out of someone. But Sam said, "No you didn't!" Leonardo asked why Sam was crying. Sam told him a long story about his big mean brother, a broken action figure, a hurt toe, soap in his eyes, bird poop on his head, no friends, and a tummy ache. After that, Leonardo decided to become a wonderful friend instead of a terrible monster. He still tried to scare his friend a little sometimes, saying, "Boo!"

summary_text: Most squirrels gather nuts and climb trees, but Mr. Peanuts is unusual. He cooks hot dogs on a tiny grill, plays “Moonlight Sonata” on the piano, and reads books aloud. Sometimes he feels lonely, so he writes to Cousin Squirrel and asks him to visit. After waiting and checking his mailbox every day, Mr. Peanuts gets a happy reply. He cleans his home, makes the bed, bakes a hazelnut chocolate cake, and gets ready for the visit. Cousin Squirrel arrives for breakfast, and they eat pancakes. Then they ride in a wagon, play chess, and pack a picnic. Cousin Squirrel adds crunchy peanuts to his peanut butter sandwiches, and Mr. Peanuts thinks they taste scrumptious. That night, they build a campfire and tell ghost stories about the haunted tree and the one-eyed owl. The next day, they eat ice cream. Mr. Peanuts and Cousin Squirrel have a wonderful time together. Having a friend makes everything twice as fun.

summary_text: Once there was a plain gray fish named Tidler. He had a big imagination and told a different tall tale every day. He said he rode a seahorse, flew with a ray, and dived with a dolphin. At school, Tidler was often late, and the other fish called his stories silly. Little Johnny Dory liked them and told them to his granny. Soon, the stories traveled from fish to fish. On Wednesday, Tidler was dreaming up his tallest story when a fishing boat caught him in a net. He escaped, but he was lost and scared in the ocean. Then he heard his own stories. Tidler followed them from anchovies to a shrimp, a whale, a herring, an eel, a lobster, a seal, a starfish, and a place. The place led him to Granny Dory. Tidler swam back to school at 3. “The story led me home again,” he said. Little Johnny Dory told it to a writer, who wrote it down.

They crush the stone to make new concrete, shred the wood to make mulch, and sort the steel so it can be used again. They load the trucks with the junk and drive it away. After that, they build the hut and put in the monkey bars. At the end, everyone joins the fun, runs, climbs, and plays. They give three cheers because the job is done.

summary_text: Hansel and Gretel lived with their father, a poor woodcutter, and their stepmother in a house near a wood. Because there was no more food or money, the stepmother said they must leave the children in the middle of the wood. Hansel heard her and got pebbles. The next day, when the family went into the woods, Hansel dropped the pebbles on the path. Their father told them to wait while he and the stepmother collected wood. The children followed the pebbles home, but the stepmother was angry and wanted them taken deeper into the wood. She locked the door so Hansel could not get more pebbles. The next day Hansel dropped breadcrumbs, but the birds ate them. Hansel and Gretel wandered in the wood until they found a house made of sweets and cakes. A witch lived there and locked Hansel in a cage. She wanted to cook him in her fire. Gretel tricked the witch, pushed her into the oven, and locked the door. She freed Hansel, they took money from the house, and they found their way home to their father.

summary_text: The story asks what it would be like to wake up with a wild animal’s nose. A tapir’s bendy proboscis grabs leaves and roots. A rabbit’s twitching nose smells danger. Its whiskers help it squeeze through spaces. An elephant’s trunk carries logs. It sprays water and picks up peanuts. A grizzly bear tracks food from far away before hibernation. A warthog sniffs and digs for roots. A saiga’s nose filters dust and warms icy air. A star-nosed mole finds food in the dark and underwater. A rhino uses its horn to guard babies. Its nose finds food and enemies. A giant anteater pokes for insects with its long nose. It breathes underwater through that nose. A horseshoe bat uses nose sounds and echoes to catch bugs. A hammerhead shark follows scents to find fish. These wild noses are useful. However, people do not need them to spray water, dig, catch flies, or swim underwater. Luckily, you do not have to choose. Your people nose helps you breathe, smell, and hold glasses. Best of all, it helps you look like you.

summary_text: Finn the Frog welcomes a child to his book and says he will make lunch. He cooks famous pasta with fire-roasted tomato sauce and Italian lily pad, but the child does not like the green stuff. Finn makes his granny’s meatloaf, but the child calls it mushy. Next, Finn serves meat soaked in pond water with whipped potatoes, but the child says it is stinky. Finn learns the child wants grilled cheese, so he makes one. He forgets to flip it, and the sandwich burns. The book catches fire, but the child helps Finn put it out. Finn makes another sandwich, but the child chooses the slightly burnt one because it is a favorite. Finn names it “Totally Toasted Cheesy Pleasy” and realizes he should ask what the child likes instead of guessing. The child burps, and Finn calls it a compliment. Finn sees that mistakes are not always bad and offers hot dessert.

summary_text: Splat was a new news cat, and it was his first real job at bedtime. He was very excited, but his mom told him he had to deliver all the papers before school and get himself up on time. Splat set his alarm for early, but when it rang at 6:00, he hit snooze. He kept doing this until 7:00, then cried because he had slept too long. He rushed downstairs, found the newspapers, and stuffed them into his bag. He dragged the papers from house to house, but he was slow and soon had no papers left for the last two houses. He was late to school too. At recess, Splat told kitten about his job. He said he was a terrible news cat. Kitten liked to tinker, so after school she and Splat made a plan and tested it. The next morning Splat tried new ways to deliver papers, then kept changing the plan again. In the end, Splat and kitten decided to work together as a newsat team.

summary_text: Dory was a young blue tang fish with short-term memory loss. Her parents, Jenny and Charlie, taught her to play hide-and-seek, but she forgot the game. When she was little, Dory became separated from them and wandered the ocean looking for her family. She met Marlin, who was searching for his son Nemo. Dory helped him, and they brought Nemo home. Later, a memory led Dory to the Jewel of Morrow Bay, California. Marlin and Nemo went with her. Dory was taken to the Marine Life Institute, where she met Hank, a seven-tentacled octopus, and her old friend Destiny. Hank helped her find her parents, but they were being sent to Cleveland. Dory found her parents, who had waited years for her. Then she helped rescue Marlin and Nemo from the truck with help from Hank and her sea friends. They drove the truck into the ocean. Back on the Great Barrier Reef, Dory lived with her family and friends. She enjoyed the view with Marlin and remembered the happy moment.

summary_text:
Bear lumbers down a small crooked trail in the deep dark woods by the strawberry veil. His tummy growls, but it is cold, so he turns back before finding a snack. The sun begins to set, and Bear feels scared. A storm starts to howl, the path gets dim, and Bear cannot find his way home. He cries by a tree and trembles in the wind.

In the warm cozy lair, Bear’s friends worry because he is still out in the storm. Mouse squeaks, Wren tweets, and the others ask if Bear should be home. They bundle up and make a search party. Badger lights a lamp, and everyone sets off together. They search high and low, trudge through the wet weather, and call, “Bear, are you there?”

Bear hears them and looks up. Ren, owl, and raven spot him and shout that it is Bear. The friends gather around him, give him bear hugs, and calm his fears. Later, they sleep in a heap, and Bear feels safe.

summary_text: It was a warm day at the beach. Chase and Rubble played catch when they heard a tiny cry from the water. A kitten was stuck on a toy boat and floating away. Rubble and Chase ran to Ryder at the lookout. Ryder called the Paw Patrol to action. Marshall, Skye, Rocky, and Zuma came to help. Ryder saw the kitten on the screen and said Zuma should use his hovercraft and Skye should fly to find her. Zuma splashed across Adventure Bay, and Skye looked from above. The kitten jumped onto Zuma’s head, then accidentally hit the hovercraft controls and sent it racing around the bay. Ryder jumped on board, stopped the engine, and picked up the shivering kitten. He took her back to dry land. Later, at Katie’s Pet Parlor, the pup and kitten learned the kitten was named Precious and belonged to a little girl. Chase followed the purple ribbon scent to town, and Marshall used his ladder to reach Precious in the Bell Tower. Ryder caught Marshall, and Precious landed safely in her owner’s arms.

summary_text: One winter morning, George rode through the forest in his yellow truck to look for fire sticks for the cabin stove. He saw Mr. Snowman and asked if everything was all right. Mr. Snowman said he was worried about the birds because the snow covered everything and they could not dig for worms. George said he had an idea and hurried home. In the kitchen, he baked seed cookies for the birds from mashed bananas and sesame seeds. His mom asked what he was doing, and George said the birds would love them. Then he loaded the warm cookies into his trailer and drove back to the snowman. Mr. Snowman thanked him and said George had a heart full of kindness. George laughed and said the birds had tummies full of seeds. The next morning, George saw that the snow was gone and the birds could find food again. After that, whenever it snowed, George brought seed cookies so the birds never went hungry.

summary_text: Taco is a 17-year-old cat who has a warm home, good food, and humans who love him. When he was a tiny kitten, a man threw him from a car near a Mexican restaurant, and Taco landed in a bush. He was trapped there for hours in the cold rain until he heard someone coming. Big hands reached into the bush, picked him up, and carried him to a warm car. A girl hugged him, took him home, and fed him from a bottle until he grew stronger. Taco became a happy, brave cat and enjoyed many adventures with his humans. He walked on a leash, went to the lake for the 4th of July, wore costumes for Halloween, and decorated the Christmas tree. One day, his humans brought home a dirty yellow kitten named Bean from under a dumpster. Taco was upset at first, but after his human reminded him of his own past, he shared a toy with Bean and decided to be a good big brother.

summary_text: The night before Thanksgiving, the family got ready for a big meal. Mom baked three pies: pecan, pumpkin, and apple surprise. The children went to bed thinking about turkey legs. The next morning, they watched the parade on TV. Relatives came by taxi, airplane, train, and car. The children helped set up the tables with silverware, chairs, and the kids’ table. The turkey went in the oven. More cousins arrived, and the children greeted them by name. They played in the room, made pilgrim hats and shoe buckles, and performed a skit. Uncle Norm called to say he was stuck in a storm. Later, Mom cooked yams, cranberry jelly, and honey baked hams. The children played outside and got hungry. When the timer rang, the turkey was done. Dad dropped it, but the children caught it on a platter. Grandpa told them to carve it. Uncle Norm arrived, and everyone sat down to eat. They were thankful to be together, and the next day they ate leftover food.

summary_text: It's Halloween, and Pete the Cat is excited to go trick-or-treating in his superhero costume. Pete hopes nothing too spooky happens, but his dad brings flashlights, and they go outside. At the next house, Pete finds a scarecrow and meets Mrs. Gold, the crossing guard, in an awesome, spooky-but-not-too-spooky costume. Then Pete and Callie see glowing jack-o-lanterns and get one piece of candy from Pete's teacher. Something behind them is their friend Emma, "not spooky, but groovy." Pete's dad says they will visit one last house. A spooky ghost scares Pete, but it is Grandma. Pete and Callie get treats and hugs. Trick-or-treating was not too spooky after all. It was full of sweet surprises. Happy Halloween!

summary_text:
Long ago, a village stood beside Lake Ontario. In a great wigwam lived an invisible being whom only his sister could see. She said a woman could marry him only if she had seen him.

A poor man had three daughters. His cruel older daughters made the youngest sit by the fire, burning and scarring her. They called her “rough-face girl” and laughed at her.

The older sisters wore fine clothes and claimed they could see the invisible being, but they could not answer questions about his bow and sled runner. They went home ashamed.

Rough-face girl had only broken shells, birch bark, and old moccasins. She made clothes and walked bravely to the wigwam. She saw the invisible being in the rainbow, the Milky Way, and the beauty of earth and sky.

They say Pig’s plans and Eagle’s excitement helped them work harder, and they agree they could not do it without each other.

summary_text: Riley was happy at school during playtime. She built a colorful City with blocks. It had roads, houses, trees, and two tall towers. Then Parker knocked over one tower by accident while moving a tree. Riley got roaring mad. She threw a block and knocked down the other tower too. Mr Rex asked how she felt and told her it was okay to feel angry, but throwing things could hurt someone. He showed Riley how to calm down by closing her eyes, taking deep breaths, counting to 10, shaking her hands, stretching her arms, and thinking about something happy. Riley calmed down and thought about riding her bike. Parker said sorry, and Riley said sorry too. Mr Rex said they could build the towers again. Riley and Parker built a new tower together, and this one was even taller. Riley felt happy again.

Then they plug in the lights, and the pine tree becomes a Christmas tree. Everyone gathers to sing and celebrate at night.

summary_text: On Day One, Akiak and her team began the 1,151-mile Iditarod race from Anchorage to Nome. Ten-year-old Akiak had led seven races but never won, and she wanted to win her last race. With Mick guiding the sled, Akiak led the dogs safely through mountains, snow, and icy trails. The team moved into first place, but deep snow hurt Akiak’s paw. Mick sent her to be flown home, yet she escaped before the plane left. Akiak followed the trail alone through a blizzard, hiding in a snowdrift until morning. She passed through Unalakleet and Shaktoolik, escaped people who tried to catch her, and found food at Koyuk and Elim. Hungry and tired, she kept chasing the team. summary_text: A big crocodile lived in a river deep in the forest. He was selfish and shouted that the river was his. He told all the forest animals to stay away or he would eat them. Because of this, the river had no fish, tadpoles, frogs, crabs, or crayfish, and the animals went far away to drink water. One morning, the forest heard a loud groaning sound. The animals saw the crocodile lying on his back in pain and holding his swollen jaw. They watched from far away and did not help. Then a little mouse came to the crocodile. The mouse climbed onto him, went into his open mouth, and pulled out a bad tooth. The crocodile felt better at once. He thanked the mouse, gave him a juicy nut, and promised to help with his teeth. Soon they became friends. The crocodile invited all the animals to drink and bathe in the river, and the river filled with life again.

He would not shave half his head like the other boys, even when his father offered him five dollars. He had no friends and was often chased by tormentors. Every day his mother asked what he learned at school. One day Wesley realized he could use what he learned to make a summer project. He decided to grow his own food crop and found his own civilization.

He turned over a patch of ground in his yard, and after a windy night, plants began to grow. The plant made fruit, roots, leaves, bark, and fibers that Wesley used for food, drink, clothes, oil, and tools. He made a hat, a robe, a sundial, new games, and even a new language. He named his land Westlandia. By the end of summer, Wesley had a whole civilization, and when he went back to school in September, he had no shortage of friends.

They worked day and night until almost no forest was left. Greta saw that the animals were sad and scared, so she decided to help them. The next day she stood in the middle of the forest with a sign that said, “Stop.” For three days the giants walked past her. On the fourth day, a little boy joined her, and then more people and animals came too. Greta told the giants they had hurt the forest. The crowd also spoke up. The giants felt ashamed, said sorry, and promised to do better. They stopped cutting trees and began gardening, cooking, repairing, tidying, and sharing. Soon the forest became beautiful again.

summary_text: Ruby loved being Ruby. She liked swinging high and exploring faraway places, even the bottom of the garden. One day, Ruby found a small worry. At first she barely noticed it, but each day it grew bigger. It was there at breakfast, at school, and at bedtime. No one else could see it, so Ruby tried to act normal. But the worry stopped her from doing the things she loved. Ruby began to worry about the worry, and it grew enormous. It filled the kitchen, the school bus, and the cinema. Ruby thought she might never feel happy again. Then she saw a boy sitting alone in the park with a worry beside him. Ruby talked to him, and his worry shrank. Ruby talked about her own worry too, and it got smaller and smaller until it was gone. Ruby felt like herself again, and later worries did not stay for long.

Arthur saw erased letters: f, r, and a. He guessed Francine. At the movie, Francine smiled. Arthur asked her to close her eyes and count to 10. She asked if she could open them.

summary_text:
Once there was a busy triangle. It held up roofs, supported bridges, made music, caught wind for sailboats, and became pie and sandwich slices. Its favorite job was slipping into place when people put hands on hips, so it heard the latest news and told friends.

One day, it wanted more sides and angles. The Shape Shifter changed it into a quadrilateral. It did new jobs, especially being book pages that taught it stories for friends. Soon it wanted more again. It became a pentagon, then a hexagon, and then many more shapes. The pentagon heard secrets but could not tell friends. The hexagon loved a beehive, but friends felt ignored.

At last, the many-sided shape rolled down a hill, crashed into fences and trees, and felt dizzy, lonely, and sad. It asked to be a triangle again. The Shape Shifter changed it back. The triangle was happy, did its old jobs, heard the latest news, and told friends. Its friends were glad it was back.

Soon Francine Pallet from Animal Control came to 54 Decoo Drive. She looked for the pig, while Mercy later went to a tea party with Stella and Frank. In the end, Francine found Mercy, and everyone came back together.

Christopher Robin remembers other adventures, but Pooh does not remember them well, so he likes hearing the stories again. Christopher Robin carries Pooh away, and Pooh bumps up the stairs behind him.

summary_text: A little old lady who was not afraid of anything went out from her cottage one windy afternoon to gather herbs, spices, nuts, and seeds in the forest. She stayed out so long that it became dark. On the path home, she met two big shoes that went clomp clomp. She told them to get out of her way and kept walking. Then she met a pair of pants that went wiggle wiggle, a shirt that went shake shake, two white gloves that went clap clap, and a tall black hat that went nod nod. Each time, she said she was not afraid and walked faster. Near her cottage, she found a very big orange pumpkin head that went boo boo. This time she ran home and locked her door. Later, she opened the door and saw all the things again. The pumpkin head said they came to scare her, but she was not afraid. She whispered to the pumpkin head, and the next morning the pumpkin head and the other things were in her garden, scaring away the crows.

summary_text: In 1959, twenty-year-old Steve Satlow learns that his father is seriously ill. Steve races to get help, but his father dies. While mourning, Steve finds a box of childhood treasures and a letter his father wrote two years earlier. The letter reminds Steve that his father loved him deeply and that family, faith, and friendship can help people through difficult times. A ticket from the 1948 Dodgers home opener brings back happy memories. The story then returns to 1948, when eight-year-old Steve eagerly follows the Brooklyn Dodgers and admires Jackie Robinson, the first African-American player in modern Major League Baseball. Steve worries about Jackie’s weight and Pete Reiser’s injury, while also hoping to attend opening day. However, Steve keeps getting into trouble at school. After he and his friend Senna push their teacher, Miss Malakin, into a hedge, Steve is suspended for ten days and loses his chance to attend the Dodgers’ opening game.

summary_text: Katie was a big red crawler tractor in the city of Giapolis. She had a bulldozer in summer and a snowplow in winter. She worked hard on the roads and liked the toughest jobs. One time, she even pulled a steamroller out of a pond. People said, “Nothing can stop her.” One winter, snow began as a drizzle, then rain, then deep snow. The truck plows went out first, but the snow got deeper and the wind made big drifts. Soon the roads were blocked, and the city stopped. Schools, stores, trains, mail, police, and even the doctor and fire department could not move. Then Katie went out. She plowed the city center, helped the police, the postmaster, the telephone and electric workers, the water department, the doctor, and the fire chief. She also cleared the airport runways. At last she finished the side streets and went home to rest.

As the penguins travel onward, the iceberg begins to melt quickly. Rossy tells Gasper that he must swim, reminding him that he is the captain. Encouraged by Rossy and their new friends, Gasper bravely jumps into the freezing water and follows her. They finally reach home and reunite with their families. Gasper feels proud, but says he could not have completed the dangerous adventure without his trusty first mate, Rossy.

summary_text: Ruby Bridges was born in a poor cabin near Tyler Town, Mississippi. When her father lost his job picking crops, the family moved to New Orleans in 1957. Ruby's father became a janitor, and her mother cared for the children by day and cleaned floors at night. In 1960, a judge ordered four Black girls to attend two white elementary schools. Six-year-old Ruby was sent to William Franz Elementary School. On her first day, angry white people stood outside with signs and shouted at her. Federal marshals had to escort her into school because the police would not help. Ruby went into an empty classroom with only her teacher, Mrs. Henry, but she kept smiling and learning. Each day she walked through the crowd, prayed for the people who hated her, and came to class ready to work. Later, two white boys and then more children joined her. By second grade, the mobs stopped trying to keep her out. Ruby finished Franz School, graduated from high school, and later started the Ruby Bridges Educational Foundation.

summary_text: Some stories say mermaids sing to sailors and cause storms, but this book says those ideas come from mistakes and superstition. It explains that mermaids are close relatives to humans and live in family groups called pods. They live in many places around the world, in seas, rivers, lakes, mountain streams, and desert water holes. Mermaids are built for speed and have tails, webbed fingers, and smooth skin with markings that help them hide in water. Their hair can be many colors, and they spend time grooming and braiding one another’s hair. Mermaids love music and shiny things. They usually stay near the water’s surface in warm sunlight and dive only to hunt for food. They eat plants, small animals, fish, and other sea life. They also make things like nets, hooks, hair pins, and combs. Mermaids sleep on rocks or float upright in the ocean, often near sperm whales.

summary_text: Dusty is a little racing plane who cannot race because his engine is damaged. While his friends look for parts, Dusty trains to become a firefighter at Piston Peak National Park. He learns to scoop water and drop fire retardant, but he makes mistakes because he does not listen and is afraid to use his broken engine. During a dangerous fire, Dusty admits that he may never race again. Blade tells him that giving up could mean not saving lives. Dusty decides to help. He flies through smoke and falling rocks, fills his pontoons, and drops water on a burning bridge to save two vehicles. His engine breaks, but Maru repairs it with spare parts and gives Dusty a new engine. Dusty earns his firefighter certification. He learns that racing is not everything and becomes a hero both as a racer and as a firefighter.

summary_text: Farmer Bailey was driving home when he hit something in the road. He thought it was a deer, but it was a man lying there. The man woke up scared, tried to run, and fell down. Mr. Bailey helped him into the truck and took him home. Mrs. Bailey made him comfortable on the parlor sofa, and Katie saw that he wore strange leather clothes. The doctor said the man had lost his memory and had a bump on his head. He stayed with the Baileys, and they gave him clean clothes, dinner, and work in the fields. He learned quickly and never seemed tired. He watched the geese fly south and looked worried when he saw the green trees around the farm while trees to the north had already turned red and orange. Soon he became upset, left in his old clothes, and disappeared. After that, every autumn the trees around the Bailey farm stay green for a week, then turn bright overnight, and the farmhouse windows show the words, “See you next fall.”

summary_text: A boy went to a concert with his sister, mother, and father at a band shell next to the zoo. The summer air was warm, and the music went on so long that he fell asleep in his seat. Then the conductor became very upset because wild animals were storming the stage. The lions, elephants, bears, raccoons, monkeys, bison, camel, yak, bonobo, ferret, jackal, hippo, tigers, and goats took the instruments and played them. The audience stayed calm, but the boy was frightened. After the animals finished, they bowed, left the stage, took off their fancy clothes, and went back to their cages. Then the boy’s sister told him to wake up or they would leave him behind. The story says never play music next to the zoo and do not fall asleep when an orchestra plays.

He spoke to Mr. Smith, watched the newsstand, helped Mr. Todd by finding Melanie Todd, and baked brownies and made lemonade for everyone. Later, Mr. Goober explained that the package had gone to the wrong house. Mr. Hatch returned the heart box and the card, then went back to being quiet and sad. After that, the neighbors talked about all the good things he had done. On Saturday morning they surprised him with hearts, candy, streamers, and a sign that said, “Everybody loves Mr. Hatch!” Mr. Hatch cried a little, then smiled and laughed again.

The pie bakes in the oven, and our tree has grown an apple pie.

The pirates tried to run, but their pants fell around their feet, so they could not go far. In the end, the pirates danced and took treasure home, and they learned to check that their pants elastic is in place.

In a little clearing, he looked at the moon. A cricket told him that different creatures may need different songs. The cricket played his violin, and Gerald listened to the grass, trees, and branches in the breeze. Soon Gerald’s hoofs shuffled, his neck swayed, and his tail swished. He threw his legs sideways, did a backward somersault, and leapt into the air. “I am dancing!” he cried. The other animals came and watched in amazement. They called him the best dancer and asked how he learned. Gerald bowed and said, “We all can dance when we find music that we love.”

summary_text: Pete the Cat goes to the toy store and sees a new robot shark toy called a Sharkbot. He really wants it, but he has no money. At home, Pete checks his bank and sees it is almost empty. He looks out the window and sees snow. Pete shovels snow for his neighbors, and Grumpy Toad’s dad pays him. Pete wants hot cocoa, but he saves his money and makes cocoa at home. He counts his money, but it is still not enough, so he puts it in his bank. When the snow melts, Mom pays Pete for helping plant flowers. Pete wants to buy a movie ticket, but he saves his money and watches a movie at home. He keeps saving through a lemonade stand, helping Grandma, and making choices to spend less. At last, Pete has enough money, buys the Sharkbot, and is happy. Then he wants a rocket racer too, and he knows saving up is cool.

That night, the child thinks about it and decides it is special to be unique, and likes their own hair and body just as they are.

Children ask to ride him and play games. Benny tries hide-and-seek, but the children find him each time. At the end of the day, Benny returns to the museum because he is needed there. Danny goes home alone, happy about their wonderful day.

Soon, they make a wonderful basket for the Easter Bunny. Pete gives it to him, and everyone is happy. They promise to make him a basket every Easter. Sharing is the sweetest gift.

summary_text: Storms happen in the atmosphere, the blanket of air around Earth. When the air changes fast and hard, we call it weather, and very violent weather is a storm. Thunderstorms are powerful storms that can bring huge amounts of rain, hail, lightning, and thunder. They begin when warm, wet air rises from the ground and meets cool, dry air. Tiny water drops form clouds, and the cloud can grow very tall and wide. Inside the storm, water drops bump together and grow bigger. He loved learning about being a leaf and did well in wind resistance, photosynthesis 101, and changing colors in autumn. But when the final exam came, Lance felt afraid because the test would make him fall from the top of his tree to the grass below. He was jealous of his neighbor Doug, an evergreen, because Doug stayed on his branch all winter.

When autumn arrived, the other leaves let go and fell, but Lance stayed on the tree and made excuses. His classmates noticed he was scared. The days grew colder, and Lance tried to stay up all winter like Doug. His teacher told him it was okay to be scared and helped him talk about his worries. Lance saw that the leaves below were safe and having fun in leaf piles and crafts. He took a deep breath, let go, and floated gently down. He passed the test and rejoined the others below.

summary_text: At the beginning, JoJo felt very alone because she had no friends. She saw that Mama Duck had ducklings, White Kitty had friends, and the birds and dragonflies stayed close together. Later, JoJo met Ned and asked him to be her friend. They had adventures together. When Ned moved away, JoJo asked Puddles to help him, and Puddles introduced Ned to Sunny. After that, JoJo made many new friends every winter.

summary_text: Kermit was an old crab who lived alone in a rocky castle in Monterey Bay. Because food was scarce, he became selfish and grumpy. He collected everything he found, even things he could never use, until his cave was packed. One day, a shiny tin can tricked Kermit into leaving the bay. A dog grabbed him and tried to bury him, but a boy stopped the dog and carried Kermit safely back to the sea. Kermit wanted to thank the boy, so he tried to help him catch a fish. Instead, a huge fish pulled Kermit far into the ocean. There, Kermit escaped a shark by hiding inside an old treasure chest filled with gold. He carried the gold to his cave, then asked a pelican to help him find the boy. The pelican delivered gold to the boy’s poor family, who used it for toys, bicycles, and a television.

smell their feet,
rock back,
drag them,
swing them,

and go on strike.
They write letters asking for respect and kindness.
In the morning, the children cannot find their chairs.
They stand all day,
and some fall when they forget.
Soon, standing is not fun,
even though they can do their schoolwork.
The children write letters back.
They say they are sorry
and promise not to rock on the chairs or fart.
They say chairs help them rest,
feel comfortable,
and focus
while learning math,
studying the planets,
and doing art.
The chairs miss the children,
so they return.
The children are kind
and keep their promise.

Lightning liked the attention, but he liked his friends Mater and Sally most. Sally asked Lightning to look out for Mater while she was away, because the Gravel Pit was dangerous. Mater then led Lightning to fun, but risky places. He raced over a grassy hill, drove backward down a dirt road, and then went to the Gravel Pit. Lightning followed because he wanted to keep Mater safe. At the pit, they heard an angry bulldozer tell them to stop playing there. The next day, Mater took Lightning back and showed him the rails in the pit. Lightning tried the ride too. Later, Mater went one more time and got stuck hanging by his toe cable. Big Bull woke up and helped free him, but Mater’s toe cable was broken.

When Sally returned, she was upset. Lightning said he would show them safe fun instead.

He hid in the bushes and shouted, and the children laughed. They kept playing this trick on each other many times, and Mr. Malouf stayed silly even when he was old.

Everyone makes a circle, sings, and talks about being thankful. Then they eat, play music, roast marshmallows, and finally walk home together along a candlelit path.

summary_text: Patricia Bath grew up in Harlem, New York, loving science and learning from her family. Her mother gave her a chemistry set, and Patricia decided she wanted to become a doctor and help sick and poor people. Many people believed doctors should be men, and the nearby high school was only for white children with money. Patricia traveled by train, finished high school in three years, and continued to college and medical school. She noticed that Black patients were blind twice as often as white patients, especially in places where money was scarce. Patricia taught students about eyes and started an eye-doctor training program. She then studied lasers in Europe and invented a laser probe that helped patients see again for many more years. She also created a place that believed healthy vision was everyone’s right. Patricia wanted to help people more than she wanted fame.

summary_text: Danny Day says he has a strange secret: he lives every day twice. His first day is called a discard day. Sticky Danny goes to school on time, does chores, avoids trouble, and eats less junk food. The power is not always fun. Moving to a new home means Danny must spend four days behind a truck instead of two. When he was younger, his parents thought he was strange, but a therapist helped them understand. Danny does not know why this happens, though he wonders if his birthday has a clue.

Hannah threw it aside, but it came alive and asked her to go to the zoo. Wearing her father’s hat and coat, the gorilla carried Hannah through the trees. The zoo was closed, but they climbed over the wall and visited the gorillas, orangutang, and chimpanzee. Hannah thought the orangutang and chimpanzee were beautiful but sad. Then they went to the cinema, ate, and danced on the lawn. The gorilla took Hannah home and promised to see her tomorrow. In the morning, Hannah saw the toy gorilla and smiled. She told her father about the night. He wished her a happy birthday and asked if she wanted to go to the zoo. Hannah was very happy.

summary_text: Mike is called “mixed up Mike,” but he says he is not mixed up at all. He has wild, curly hair and likes to move fast. His daddy is deep brown, and his mom is rich cream and honey. When Mike is with both parents, some people stare and ask why they do not match. Mike’s mom and dad tell him he is a blend of dark and light and that he was made just right. Mike also hears kids at school ask him to choose who he wants to be with. He says he likes fun with everyone and does not want to pick one race. If people care too much about his hair and want it straight, he says, “It’s my hair, don’t touch.” In the end, Mike says he is a beautiful blend of dark and light and that he is just right.

summary_text: Aladdin, Jasmine, Rajah, and Abu saw the biggest parade of the year. They watched a snake charmer, a fire-eater, peacocks, elephants, and tigers. Jasmine showed everyone that Rajah could balance fruit and cut it into pieces with his claws. Aladdin suggested that Abu and Rajah join the parade while he and Jasmine returned to the palace. Soon, Abu came back upset and showed them that the parade people had taken Rajah. Aladdin and Jasmine flew after the parade on the magic carpet. They crashed into clotheslines, then ran across rooftops until they found Rajah being put into a cage. Jasmine hugged him and removed his collar, but the parade master said the tiger was not hers. Jasmine tossed Rajah a melon, and he sliced it with his claws. The parade master understood his mistake and let Rajah go. Jasmine was happy to have her friend back.

summary_text: Nikolai wants to be a good person, but he does not know the answers to three questions: When is the best time to act? Who is most important? What is the right thing to do? His friends give different answers, so Nikolai visits Leo, an old turtle. Leo is digging a garden. Nikolai helps him, and soon a storm begins. Nikolai finds a panda with an injured leg and carries her to Leo’s house. Then he searches for her frightened baby and brings it inside, warm and safe. The next morning, the panda and her baby are well. Nikolai is happy, but he still wants the answers. Leo explains that the important time was always the present moment. The important ones were the people Nikolai was helping, and the right thing was to do good for the person beside him. Nikolai learns that helping others now is what matters most.

summary_text: On a bright spring day, winter snow melts and the world outside changes. Grass grows, and trees get new leaves. Clouds float in the breeze and change shape. Then gray clouds bring a little rain, so an umbrella is needed to stay dry. Raindrops fall into puddles for splashing. After that, ducklings follow their mother and go quack. Bees buzz and toads croak, making sounds together. When the rain stops, the air smells fresh and sweet. Flowers bloom, and they can be sniffed. Next, the garden has vegetables growing in it, like cabbages, radishes, carrots, lettuce, and green peas. These are ready for an afternoon snack. Then the sun shines, and a bright rainbow appears in the sky. The story ends by saying spring is a season full of delight.

summary_text: Jack could not sleep early one morning, so he looked at his notebook and read the list of strange things that had happened the day before. He and his sister Annie had found a tree house in the woods, found many books inside it, wished on pictures, and traveled to the time of dinosaurs before coming home. Annie came to his room and saw that Jack had not written about the gold medallion or the letter M on it. She also asked about the magic person who may have built the tree house. Jack said he was only writing facts, but Annie wanted to go back and find out more. Jack worried, but Annie went with him anyway. They dressed quietly, slipped outside, and ran into Frog Creek Woods. In the dark tree house, they found the books still there. Annie opened a castle book, and the wind began to blow. The tree house spun, and they traveled to a castle in the mist.

summary_text: Dave lived about 200 years ago and was a slave. He worked with clay, which came from dirt mixed with water from the river. He carried heavy clay to his spinning potter’s wheel and threw as much as 60 pounds at a time. He kicked the wheel fast and shaped the wet clay with his hands and thumbs. He made jars so large that he could not wrap his arms around them. Then he rolled long ropes of clay and added them to the jar to make it stronger. After that, he mixed wood ash and sand to make a brown glaze that would last a long time. Before the jar hardened, Dave used a stick to write words on it: “I wonder where is all my relation friendship to all and every nation.” He made pots and left messages in them, so people would know he was there.

summary_text: Sebastian says he can handle anything. He tells about many times when he feels hard feelings. When his best friend is mad, Sebastian feels sad, but he can give a hug, try to make him laugh, or draw a picture. When adults do not listen, he feels frustrated, and he can say, “Excuse me,” write a letter, or tell someone else. When his sister bothers him, he feels mad, and he can ask her to stop, move away, or make a joke. When he cannot find his shoe, he feels annoyed, and he can look for it or wear another pair. When he wants a pet but cannot have one, he feels disappointed, and he can pretend, make a pet, or play with a friend’s pet. Sebastian also feels ashamed, upset, discouraged, cranky, and miserable at other times, but he finds ways to handle each problem. In the end, he says he can handle all of these feelings.

summary_text: Derek, a longtime photo librarian, is sorting old newspaper photographs before retirement. He finds a picture from 1962 showing police gathered around the body of Lucia Rennicks, a murdered schoolgirl. In the background stands a strange, black-covered figure staring toward the photographer. Years later, Derek finds another photograph of a different murder in Candlewood Park. The same figure appears in the same position, even though the second picture was taken eleven years later. Derek becomes convinced that the photographs show the Candlewood Park strangler and that the killings may be connected. He decides to report the evidence, but first discovers that young photographer Nick has gone to the same part of the park. Derek races to warn him. Before he can arrive, his car is struck by a lorry and destroyed by a passing train. Meanwhile, Nick finds the mysterious figure in the park and realizes it is an old, rusted Boer War statue. Just then, a hand grabs the back of his neck.

They imagined diving at Niagara Falls, sledding in Switzerland, visiting Tahiti, Paris, Venice, Moscow, and Pluto. Pete eventually became upset because his simple life had changed. When he told Pickles to leave, a pipe broke and the house flooded. Pete escaped through a window, but Pickles could not fit. Pete realized he could not live without her. He held on and breathed for Pickles until they were rescued. The friends slept, then woke to pick blueberries on Pluto.

summary_text: Finn lived by the sea and remembered his grandfather, who had told him stories about a place where the ocean meets the Sky. To honor Grandpa on his 90th birthday, Finn built a boat for a long trip they had planned together. After he rested for a little while, the boat rocked, and Finn knew the journey had started. He felt lonely on the Open Sea, until a great golden fish came to him. Finn asked the fish where ocean meets Sky. The fish answered and led Finn to the Library Islands, where birds sat with books. Finn and the fish also visited an island of giant shells and a sea of moon jellies. Then Finn saw many ships and a huge whale, and his boat seemed to lift from the water. The golden fish swam toward the moon, and Finn followed, wanting to say goodbye and ask more questions. Then his mother called him for dinner, and she had made Grandpa’s dumplings. Finn looked out at the sea and remembered the magical place.

summary_text: On Christmas Eve, Marie and Fritz waited outside a bright ballroom and peeped through the keyhole. They smelled spruce tree, puff pastry, and music. At last the doors opened, and Fritz ran to the gifts while Marie looked at the room and the tall Christmas tree with candles, ribbons, and apples. Their godfather, Judge Drosselmeyer, showed Marie a wooden doll called the Nutcracker. He cracked a walnut in the doll’s mouth, and Marie loved the toy and hugged it. Fritz wanted to try it too, but he used a very hard nut and broke the Nutcracker’s jaw. Marie took the doll away, bandaged his jaw with a ribbon, and sang to him until she fell asleep under the tree.

summary_text: Straw was part of a big family with many colors and stripes. He had many friends, and he loved to be first. One day, Straw got a bad brain freeze from drinking too fast. His head hurt, and he felt sad. A glassmate saw him and asked him to play. She showed Straw how to blow bubbles. Straw tried it and learned quickly. He laughed and played with the bubbles. Then his friend told him that not everything is a race and that some things should be savored. Straw had not thought about that before. That night, after bedtime story, Straw talked about the strawberry swirls in the whipped cream and the rainbow inside a tiny bubble. He stayed in bed and thought about the day until he fell asleep. After that, Straw still sometimes wanted to be first, but most of the time he wanted to make good things last.

All the animals went to find Hippo in the hot dry grass. Monkey climbed onto Hippo’s snout and asked what was wrong. Hippo groaned. Zebra noticed his breath was hot and he had a fever. The animals pushed Hippo toward the river, and his tooth popped out. The animals helped him stand up. Hippo said thank you, but now his head hurt.

Kora washed her hands and helped gather ingredients like chicken, vegetables, soy sauce, and noodles. She soaked the rice noodles, shredded cooked chicken, and watched Mama chop and cook the vegetables with garlic and ginger. At dinner, the family returned, tasted the food, and praised Kora’s work. Daddy said it tasted like L’s soup, and Kora felt proud.

summary_text: Every afternoon, giraffe and zebra walked together to the watering hole. But one day giraffe could not go. He called for zebra and, after looking around, zebra found him high in a tree, holding on tightly. Giraffe whispered that he had seen a spider and was scared it might crawl on him or chase him. Zebra told giraffe that he was bigger, stronger, and faster than the spider, and asked him to come down. Giraffe still felt worried and embarrassed. Zebra did not leave. He waited beside the tree as the sun went down. At last giraffe slowly climbed down and thanked zebra for staying with him. Zebra said that if something bothers a friend, it is not silly. Then they started toward the watering hole. Soon giraffe saw a spider walking alone. Giraffe felt brave and asked if it wanted to join them, but the spider quickly ran up a tree. Zebra said the spider was scared now, and giraffe stayed with his friend.

On Thanksgiving morning, everyone came, but too many guests arrived for the table and there was no room inside. Franklin saw what to do. The family and all the guests carried food, tables, and chairs outside and ate in the field. Everyone had a happy Thanksgiving, and Grandma and Grandpa later called to hear all about the new tradition.

After that, Gustavo’s life changed, and everyone saw how he helped and protected his friends.

summary_text: On a moonlit night, three thieves examine jewels stolen from Carlotta Grimstone. When the necklace breaks, the stones form a glowing circle and show each thief a frightening vision. One thief will be caught, another will die by water, and the first sees that two people born together will die together. A helicopter arrives, forcing the thieves to run. Two thieves escape with the moonstones, but one slips into a waterfall. Years later, March McQuinn is helping his father, Alfie, complete another jewel theft in Amsterdam. March steals a bicycle and waits outside a hotel. Alfie throws him a strange blue-white stone, then falls from the roof and dies. March escapes with the stone, grieving his father and remembering his advice. Soon, he realizes someone is following him.

summary_text: Annie thinks the magic treehouse has returned, so she and Jack hurry into Frog Creek woods before they leave for grandmother’s house. In the treehouse, they find a note from Morgan telling them to find a special magic by following a rhyme about gathering together. A book named A Feast to Remember leads them to the time of the pilgrims. The treehouse lands near Plymouth Colony in 1620, and Jack and Annie see that they look like a pilgrim boy and girl. They meet Governor Bradford, Captain Standish, Priscilla, and Squanto. When Chief Masasoid and 90 men arrive, the pilgrims worry that they do not have enough food for the feast. Jack and Annie try to help by catching eels and clams, then by working in Priscilla’s house. Jack burns the turkey by accident, but Priscilla shows them there is still plenty of food. After the feast, Squanto walks them back and teaches them how to grow corn. He also explains that he remembered what it felt like to be different and afraid, and Jack writes down the lesson to be kind to people who feel that way.

summary_text: Hamlet the pig leaned over a fence and looked at the other pigs in the mud. He asked his mother and father to read a new book to him, but his father only asked if it was a cookbook. Hamlet then showed his mother his notebook and said he had written poems. His sister and brother laughed at him because he wore a clean shirt and wrote poems. While everyone laughed, the farmer walked away from supper, and the pigs rushed across the Mud Hole shouting, “Supper! Supper! Supper!” Hamlet did not feel hungry. He noticed mud on his favorite shirt and walked away by himself. Near the farmer’s pond, he watched the rising moon and wrote more poems in his notebook. When he looked into the pond, he saw his twin reflection, whom he called Eggs. Hamlet read poems to Eggs, and the reflection seemed to answer. Then the moon and clouds changed, the reflection faded, and Hamlet heard small voices say they liked his poems and wanted him to read to them.

summary_text: Mother and father went for a sail in their boat, but the child stayed home because of a runny trunk and a sore throat. A storm came, and the boat did not return. The child sat alone in a dark room until Uncle elephant opened the door and came in. He took the child out, and they rode on a train together, eating peanuts and watching the land rush past. Uncle elephant tried to count houses, fields, and telephone poles, but everything moved too fast. At his house, he lit a lamp, and a small spider inside asked for peace, so Uncle elephant turned the lamp off and they ate supper. The next morning, he trumpeted the dawn, showed his flower garden, and the child became the prince while Uncle elephant was the king. Later, Uncle elephant told a story about a king and a prince who helped each other find their castle. The child felt sad looking at a family picture, so Uncle elephant wore all his clothes at once and made them both laugh. He wrote a song for the child, and later a telegram said mother and father had been found. Uncle elephant took the child home, and they said goodbye after one last song and piano music.

summary_text: In the middle of the night, Jason kept waking up and hearing strange sounds. Each time, he found his father sleepwalking in a different place. First, his father was on top of the refrigerator in the kitchen. Then Jason found him sleeping in the bathtub. After that, he found him asleep on top of the car in the garage. Each time Jason called, “Papa, wake up,” and his father jumped up, ran around three times, and went back to bed. Jason said the house was going crazy, and he was very tired. Later, Jason saw his father’s footprints going out into the snow on a very cold night. Jason worried his father would freeze, so he put on many warm clothes, followed the footprints, and found him by a tree. Jason could not lift him, so he got a sled and pulled him home. He then tied his father’s big toe to the bed so the sleepwalking would stop.

summary_text: In the middle of the night, Jason kept waking up and hearing strange sounds in his house. Each time he opened a door, he found his father sleepwalking in a different place. summary_text: The highlighters say they are bright and colorful and help make school pages easy to see. They add yellow ink to black and white words so important things stand out. But the students do not treat them gently. The students press them hard, push them into desks, bend and snap them, chew the ends, and often lose the caps. The highlighters also get tossed around in bins and scratched by pencils. Because of this rough treatment, their ink dries out and they stop working well. One day during recess, the highlighters choose the brightest one and write a note in big yellow letters. The note says they are tired of being treated like junk and that the highlighters are going on strike. When the students return from outdoor play, they find the note and read it quietly. They gather together and write back to say they are sorry and will treat the highlighters carefully. The highlighters agree to give them another chance, but say they will strike again if the mistreatment happens again.

summary_text: One winter morning at 6:53, Mr. McGee and his little dog Dee woke up to fresh snow and a beautiful sky. They decided to try skiing before driving all the way to Mount Snow. Not far away, a curious moose was looking for birch sticks. He saw Mr. McGee and Dee and froze in surprise. Mr. McGee could not steer and shouted for the moose to move, then yelled, “Duck!” The skis snagged on a spruce log, and Mr. McGee and Dee flew into a ravine, hanging high above the ground. Later, the moose stepped onto the skis, which bent and sprang up, sending Mr. McGee and Dee safely back to the top. Mr. McGee said they still had not really learned to ski and would let someone else use the skis for a while.

At breakfast time, his mother carries him down the hill to find food. Roo says he is not hungry, but his mother says she is hungry and asks him to hold tight. On the way, she does silly hops and misses a wide hole with mud at the bottom. She slips right into it. Roo and his mother become muddy and wet. When Roo sees his mother covered in slimy mud, he cannot help smiling. His mother is happy to see his smile.

summary_text: Bobby had a big problem at school. His teacher, Miss Kirby, stomped around and shouted, “Move it or lose it!” and “Settle down!” She said children who threw paper airplanes in class would miss recess. Bobby spent his free time in the park trying to forget his teacher troubles. One Saturday morning, while he was walking to his favorite spot, Bobby found Miss Kirby there. He wanted to run away, but he stayed. They talked in a careful way, and Bobby said hello and told her he liked her enormous hat. Then a gust of wind blew the hat away, and Miss Kirby asked Bobby to catch it. Bobby grabbed the hat and gave it back. After that, they watched ducks and quacked with them. Bobby showed Miss Kirby his favorite spot in the park, and she liked it. Bobby then flew his paper airplane, and it flew very far. By lunchtime, Bobby and Miss Kirby were happy and said goodbye. At school later, Miss Kirby still stomped and roared, but Bobby had seen her outside school too.

summary_text: Gerald the giraffe wants to dance at the jungle dance. He is tall, with a long neck, thin legs, and crooked knees. He can stand still and eat leaves, but dancing makes him fall. At the dance, the other animals move and laugh at Gerald. Gerald feels sad and walks away alone. In a quiet clearing, a little cricket tells him that different animals may need different music. The cricket plays a violin, and Gerald listens to the grass, trees, and moon. Soon, Gerald’s body begins to move. He shuffles, sways, swings his legs, spins, and jumps. Gerald discovers that he can dance. The other animals see him and are amazed. They ask how he learned to dance. Gerald dances happily and says that everyone can dance when they find music they love.

summary_text: Gerald was a tall giraffe with a long, slim neck, crooked knees, and thin legs. He could stand still and munch tree shoots, but he buckled when he ran. At Africa’s yearly jungle dance, the animals danced while Gerald felt sad because he was bad at dancing. The lions and other animals laughed and called him clumsy, so Gerald froze and walked home feeling alone. In a clearing, Gerald admired the moon. A cricket told him that different creatures may need different songs and that everything makes music. The cricket played his violin, and Gerald began to shuffle, sway his neck, swish his tail, leap, and dance. “I am dancing!” Gerald cried. The animals came back and watched with wide eyes. They called him the best dancer they had ever seen and asked how he learned. Gerald bowed, looked at the moon, and said, “We all can dance when we find music that we love.”

summary_text: It is Cupcake’s birthday, and she wants to share it with friends. She asks Muffin to help plan a party, and they take a long walk while Cupcake thinks of ideas. First, Cupcake wants a beach party with sprinkle castles and sun play, but Muffin says the beach is very hot and some friends might get drippy. Next, Cupcake thinks of a floating boat party, but Muffin says the ship might rock and soup could lose lunch. Cupcake then suggests makeovers with frosting and sprinkles, but Muffin says some friends might think that is icky. Cupcake tries musical chills, but Muffin says someone sitting down fast could get squished. Cupcake runs out of ideas and suggests the lambo with prizes. At last, she decides to rest in her garden. When she opens the gate, all her friends are there. They dance, some get a little drippy, and Cupcake gets a little squished during limbo. Still, it becomes the best birthday party anyone can remember.

That is what the zookeeper hears.

We jumped on the trampoline and later collected fireflies when it got dark. Then the yawns came. There were many yawns, and they chased us. We ran, climbed, sneaked, and hid, but the yawns caught us. I yawned, then Nudles yawned, and we kept yawning again and again. I tried to keep Nudles awake, but he only yawned. Then a slap-a-do landed on Nudles’s head. We still had more fun things on our list, but the snores arrived and danced around Nudles’s head. My eyes got heavy, and a sleepy covered me up. It was warm and safe. In the morning, Nudles was awake and smiling, and he made a new list for us.

summary_text: A child and Nana begin gardening in spring. They clear away old plants, spread compost, and plant seeds. Under the soil, earthworms, insects, and pill bugs are busy too. The seeds grow into carrots, peas, cucumbers, zucchini, tomatoes, and pumpkins. Bees, wasps, ladybugs, spiders, birds, and many other creatures visit the garden. Rain fills the soil, and roots drink the water. The child and Nana eat vegetables and watch animals find food. During summer nights, bats fly, skunks dig, and a snake eats supper. When autumn comes, pumpkins turn orange and sunflowers bow. They harvest the garden and share food with neighbors. Then frost arrives, so they cover the garden for winter. Beetles, ants, and earthworms hide below the ground. Above the soil, the garden becomes quiet, but life is still there. Under the snow, the garden sleeps and waits for warm sunshine, blossoms, and new sprouts.

summary_text: One wonderful day, Jim the chimpanzee woke up and felt that everything was wrong. The sky was too blue, the sun was too bright, and the bananas were too sweet. His friends noticed that he looked grumpy. They told him to raise his eyebrows, smile, sing, swing, roll, stroll, dance, laugh, and do many other happy things. Jim tried to smile, but he still did not feel happy inside. At last, he shouted that he was grumpy and walked away. Jim felt sorry for shouting. Then he found Norman, who was also slumped, frowning, and grumpy because he was hurt by a porcupine. Jim said that he was still grumpy, but he would probably feel better soon. Norman agreed. Jim learned that he did not have to pretend to be happy right away. He could feel grumpy for a while, and he already felt a little better.

summary_text: Rebecca Estelle grows many vegetables every spring, but she never plants pumpkins because she once had to eat pumpkins for every meal when her family had little money. One autumn, a pumpkin falls from a truck into her yard. She buries the pieces, but pumpkin vines grow there the next spring. Rebecca cuts them down, yet they grow back. She ignores them all summer, and by autumn her yard is filled with pumpkins. At first, she does not know what to do. Then she decides to give the pumpkins away. She makes pies, tarts, muffins, cakes, bread, pudding, and cookies. She also carves funny and scary faces into pumpkins and lights them with candles. People from town see the glowing pumpkins and come to visit. Rebecca shares all the treats and gives everyone a jack-o-lantern, seeds, and a pumpkin treat. She keeps only a few seeds for planting next spring.

summary_text: Every morning Sarah watches from the window as her mom goes to work and waves from the bus stop. Grandma says he may be poor and hungry. Sarah thinks about him at school and saves her snack cookie for him. She asks Mom to leave it near Saul’s store. Later the man finds the cookie and eats it. Sarah tells her friends, and they wrap more cookies. Her teacher says this is called sadaka, giving to someone who has less. Sarah and Mom also leave juice and a sandwich for the man. Soon Sarah sees his face and thinks she knows him. At a Shabbat and Hanukkah party, she learns his name is Morris Berger. After that, food is left for him every day.

summary_text: Billions of honeybees have disappeared from their colonies and failed to return. This condition is called colony collapse disorder, or CCD. Because honeybees pollinate about one-third of U.S. crops, their disappearance could threaten the production of fruits and vegetables. Scientists have considered several possible causes, including overcrowded hives, stress, lack of pollen, parasites, and pesticides. Researchers in Montana found both a fungus and a virus in every empty hive they tested, while unaffected hives did not have the same problem. Bees might survive either infection alone, but the combination could be deadly. Other scientists think several factors may work together by weakening bees’ immune systems. Pesticides are another possible cause. Studies show that some pesticides can change bee behavior, causing sick bees to become lost. Scientists have not proved that pesticides directly cause CCD, but the chemicals may weaken bees enough to allow infections. Research continues to find the exact cause and a way to save the bees.

summary_text: Billions of honeybees have disappeared from their colonies and failed to return, causing colony collapse disorder (CCD). The disorder has reduced the U.S. honeybee population to about half its level 50 years ago and threatens food production because honeybees pollinate many crops. Scientists have considered overcrowded hives, lack of pollen, parasites, pesticides, a fungus, and a virus as possible causes. In Montana, researchers compared empty hives with healthy control hives and found the fungus and virus in every empty hive tested. Bees might survive either infection alone, but the combination was most certainly deadly. Other scientists are studying whether several factors weaken bees’ immune systems together. Pesticides may also harm bees: they can enter pollen, affect bees’ ability to find nectar, and cause them to become lost. Studies found many chemicals in affected hives but could not prove pesticides directly caused CCD. Investigations continue, and scientists must identify the cause before finding a cure; pesticide use should be cut back.

summary_text: George Ferris wanted to create something amazing for the 1893 Chicago World’s Fair. The Eiffel Tower had impressed the world, so George designed a giant moving wheel instead of another tall tower. He and William Gronau carefully measured the plans, but the fair’s construction chief thought the wheel would collapse. George believed that strong steel would make it safe. Finding money was difficult, so he used his savings and found investors. Workers then dug through frozen ground and dangerous quicksand before building a deep, sturdy foundation. They assembled more than 100,000 parts and finished the enormous wheel just in time. On opening day, George blew a whistle, and the wheel began turning. Riders saw Chicago, Lake Michigan, and distant states from the cars. Millions of people enjoyed the ride during the fair. The wheel survived storms and became famous as the Ferris wheel. Copies soon appeared around the world, and Ferris wheels remain popular carnival rides today.

summary_text: Before the 1893 Chicago World's Fair, organizers needed an attraction to surpass the Eiffel Tower. Mechanical engineer George Ferris designed a huge moving wheel made of strong, lightweight steel. His partner, William Gronau, helped measure the plans, but judges and lenders doubted the unusual idea. With little money, George gathered investors and ordered parts from steel mills. Workers dug through frozen ground and dangerous quicksand, then built a deep foundation and assembled more than 100,000 pieces. On June 21, 1893, the Ferris wheel opened. Its passenger cars rose 265 feet, giving riders views of Chicago, Lake Michigan, and distant states. Steam engines turned the wheel, which carried 1.5 million passengers during the fair and survived storms without repairs. At night, 3,000 electric bulbs made it glow. When the fair ended, George’s investors named the invention the Ferris wheel. Copies soon appeared around the world, and Ferris wheels remain popular rides at fairs and amusement parks.

summary_text: A little old woman and a little old man lived happily on a farm, but they were sad because they had no children. The woman made a boy from gingerbread. She shaped him, gave him eyes, a mouth, and buttons, and baked him in the oven. When she opened the oven, the gingerbread man jumped out and ran away. The gingerbread man climbed onto the fox’s tail, back, and nose as the water rose. The fox snapped each time. Soon the gingerbread man was gone.

Arlo let Spot go because that was where Spot belonged. Arlo returned to his own family and knew he had earned his mark.

The older child thinks the parents love him more. When the brother is put to bed early, staying up late is not fun because there is no one to play with. The next day, the brother sings during a phone call and knocks down the older child’s block buildings with garbage trucks. The older child also feels jealous because the cat sleeps on the brother’s bed. Then the younger brother tells his side. He thinks his older sister is a great one because she can play piano, use the can opener, care for the baby, remember phone numbers, and build block cities. He tries playing blocks alone, but it is not as much fun. At swimming, he teases his sister because he is afraid of the water, and both children feel that their parents love the other one best.

summary_text: The narrator calls his six-year-old brother “the pain” because he needs help getting ready, cries when left behind, and receives special attention. He eats poorly, makes a mess in the bathroom, and stays up late. When their parents let the narrator stay up later, he finds it boring without his brother. The next day, the brother interrupts a phone call, knocks down block buildings, and the narrator thinks his brother gets the love he wants. He thinks Mom and Daddy love his brother better because they call him lovable and say he is what they always wanted. The brother calls his older sister “the great one” and complains that she plays piano, feeds the cat, cares for the baby, remembers phone numbers, and builds block cities. He wants to be the garbage man and knocks down her buildings. When he plays with the blocks alone, he discovers it is not fun. At swimming, she can swim and dive while he is afraid to put his face in the water, so he spits water, pulls her hair, and pinches her. After their parents praise and hug her, he thinks they love her better than him.

summary_text: One day, Macy went camping with all her friends. They found a good place and worked together to pitch a tent. The tent fell down, so they tried again and again. At last, the tent stayed up. That night, the friends sang around the campfire. Then they got ready for bed. Thyro went into the tent with a flashlight. Charlie came next and watched the pegs. Tula came in after Charlie, and everyone made room for Macy. Eddie came too, so five friends were squeezed inside the tent. It was a squash and a squeeze. Soon, Cyel popped out, then Tula, Charlie, and Macy. At last, one friend was in the tent, while four friends slept under the stars. The campers said good night and slept.

summary_text: Long ago, God promised to send a special king. This king would be different from every other king. He would rescue his people and be their king forever. An angel visited Mary and told her that her baby would be this special king. Another angel told Joseph that Mary’s baby would rescue God’s people. God had promised that the king would be born in Bethlehem, so Mary and Joseph went there. Bethlehem was very busy, and the baby slept in a manger instead of a bed. That night, an angel told shepherds that God’s chosen king had been born. The shepherds hurried to Bethlehem and found the baby in the manger. Far away, wise men saw a new star. They understood that the promised king had been born, so they traveled to see him. Everything God promised came true. The baby’s name was Jesus, the new king, the rescuing king, and the forever king.

summary_text: Llama Llama goes to school and learns many things. He learns counting, writing, reading, and rules. He also learns the letters of the alphabet. He remembers some words with his brain and eyes. He writes his name too: L, L, A, M, A. Then he reads more words, like Llama Llama and love. The teacher shows him a walking sign, and the class makes a line. Llama learns that sentences make a book. He goes to the library and reads many stories there. He reads about fairy princesses, pirate kings, knights, and dragons. At the end of the day, Llama sees a stop sign, reads the word stop, and stops. School is over, and he is proud to be a reader.

summary_text: An old lady begins Thanksgiving by swallowing a whole pie, even though it is very dry. Then she swallows cider to moisten the pie. Next, she eats a roll, a squash, a salad, and a turkey. Each time, she keeps adding more Thanksgiving food and repeats that the food inside her is rumbling, mumbling, and grumbling. Then she swallows a pot, followed by a ten-layer cake. People tie rope to her feet. At last, the old lady swallows some bread and says, “I’m full.” She wishes everyone a happy Thanksgiving. The story is a funny food-filled rhyme about an old lady who keeps swallowing more and more things.

At school, Spike announces that he likes Kitten too. Spike draws a huge heart and shows off his large card. Splat feels sad because his card looks tiny, so he throws it away. Kitten secretly finds Splat's card and reads the three words, “I like you.” Then she gives Splat her own card. It says that she likes his soft fur, funny belly noise, bendy tail, and nice smell after a bath. Inside, she writes, “I like you.” Splat gets a special Valentine from Kitten.

None of the monsters scared Emma. Gabe returned and tried to frighten her, but Emma called him a fuzzy monster and kept singing. Gabe decided to stay with Emma because she was at least in bed. Then Gabe’s little sister, Stella, arrived. Stella had hiccups and liked toes. Emma became frightened by Stella, so Stella was the perfect monster for her. Emma had Stella, and Ethan had Gabe, so everything became normal again.

You can walk around a block or a yard, or simply keep still. Sounds are everywhere all the time. At the end, the child invites listeners to close the book and count how many sounds they can hear.

On the golden sand, he found a star that had washed ashore. At last, the boy had caught a star of his very own.

summary_text: One sunny spring morning, Winnie-the-Pooh was hungry and had no honey. He went to Rabbit’s tidy house and learned that bees need flowers and gardens to make honey. Pooh thought this meant gardens grow honey, so he told Piglet about a secret garden. Tigger found a good spot, and the friends asked Owl how to plant it. Owl said they needed seeds, and Rabbit gave them some. Pooh, Piglet, Tigger, Owl, Kanga, and Roo planted the seeds. They waited while plants grew and bees buzzed, but no honey appeared. Pooh found a tomato instead and wished the garden would grow honey. Rabbit came with Roo and said there was no secret: they only had to follow a bee to its hive. The bee flew into a stump, where Pooh found honey. The secret garden was not secret anymore. Pooh’s friends picked vegetables, while Pooh happily collected honey and became sticky.
