summary_text: Everyone in town knew Edua, a friendly dinosaur who played with children, helped little old ladies cross the street, and baked chocolate chip cookies. Everyone loved her except Reginald, who thought he knew everything. One day, Reginald gave a school report about extinct dinosaurs. The children said Edua could not be extinct because she was right there helping people and baking cookies. Reginald felt happy because someone had listened to him. Soon, he did not care either, and Edua continued being the friendly dinosaur everyone loved.

When the real Bruce came home, he saw the mess and became grumpy again. Everything returned to normal, except the family got twenty-six pizzas instead of sandwiches.

summary_text: Jack wanted a big pancake for breakfast. His mother said he needed to help first. Jack cut wheat and took it to the mill. He helped separate the grain and grind it into flour. Then he fed the black hen, and she laid an egg. He milked the spotted cow and got milk. With his mother’s help, he churned the cream into butter. Jack brought firewood from the woodshed and strawberry jam from the cellar. In the kitchen, his mother mixed flour, egg, and milk in a bowl. She heated butter in a pan and poured in the batter. When the pancake was golden underneath, she flipped it high into the air and back into the pan. Soon it was crisp on both sides. His mother put it on a plate and spread jam on top. Jack knew what to do next: enjoy his big pancake.

summary_text: Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta in 1929. His father was a pastor, and his mother had been a teacher. Martin loved sports, music, and reading. When he learned that white children could not play with him because he was Black, he was hurt and confused. His mother explained that Black people had once been enslaved and were still treated unfairly. Martin became a minister and later married Ketta Scott. In Montgomery, Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat, so Martin led a peaceful bus boycott. After almost a year, buses no longer had white-only sections. Martin continued peaceful protests and led the March on Washington, where he gave his “I Have a Dream” speech. He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964. In 1968, James Earl Ray shot and killed Martin in Memphis. Martin dreamed of a world without hate, prejudice, or violence.

Martin Luther King Jr. was born in 1929 in Atlanta, Georgia. As a child, he learned that Black people faced unfair treatment and white-only places because of segregation. He read about Black leaders, became an excellent student, and decided to become a minister. After studying at Morehouse College and Boston University, he married Ketta Scott and became a pastor in Montgomery, Alabama.

When Rosa Parks was arrested, Dr. King led a peaceful bus protest. He told angry followers, “We must meet hate with love.” After almost a year, buses no longer had white-only sections. In Atlanta, he led protests and the 1963 March on Washington, where he gave his “I have a dream” speech. He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964, and new laws ended legal segregation. In 1968, James Earl Ray shot Dr. King in Memphis while Dr. King supported equal pay for Black and white garbage workers. Dr. King died, dreaming of a world free of hate, prejudice, and violence.

Al and the dragon talked about eggs, nighttime, and flying. They discovered they had much in common. After that, no more knights disappeared. Al kept patrolling the walls, and he was brave, clever, and surrounded by friends.

Coach said flies could not play football, but Fly Guy could come to the game. Before the game, Buzz made Fly Guy a helmet. They practiced, planned a secret play, and made a touchdown dance. At the big game, Fly Guy sat on the bench. The Go-Getters were behind, 14 to 17, with one second left. A player was hurt, so Coach let Fly Guy play. Fly Guy flew up the quarterback's nose, and the boy dropped the ball. Buzz picked it up and scored. Fly Guy and Buzz did their touchdown dance. The team cheered, "We won! Hooray for Fly Guy!"

summary_text: Mr. Silly lived in Nonsense Land, where trees had red leaves, grass was blue, dogs wore hats, and birds flew backward. He dreamed of winning the Nonsense Cup for the silliest idea. At breakfast, he ate a strange meal, including a cornflake sandwich and an egg shell. He remembered that Mr. Ridiculous had won by wallpapering the outside of his house, and Mr. Foolish had won with a car that had square wheels. Mr. Silly thought hard, but no idea came. During a walk, he saw animals wearing funny clothes and making the wrong sounds. Then he had a wonderful idea. He bought paint and painted all the leaves of a tree green. At the cup ceremony, Mr. Muddle showed a square apple and Miss Ninkmp showed a silly teapot. But the king and crowd were amazed by the green tree. Mr. Silly won the Nonsense Cup because his idea was the silliest.

summary_text: One morning, somebody put a chocolate chicken in the bird bath. Max loved it, but Ruby said they must first have an egg hunt. Whoever found the most eggs would get the chocolate chicken. Max looked near a mud puddle, but he found no egg. Ruby found a big yellow egg. Max looked again and found acorns, while Ruby found a blue egg. Ruby told Max to keep looking. Max went with Ruby. She found red, gold, turquoise, and lavender eggs. Max found a spoon and some ants, then made ant and acorn pancakes. Ruby counted her eggs and said she would win. Max hid by the bird bath. Ruby looked for him. While she searched, Max ate the chicken’s tail, head, and wings. Ruby offered him half, but Max came out after eating most of it. Ruby was upset, and Max said he loved her.

summary_text: Matty loves glue at home with Dad and Mom, but his art teacher says, “Too much glue never dries” and “Glue raindrops, not puddles!” In art class, Matty uses the fullest glue bottles and makes a big sticky mess with sequins and googly eyes. Then he rolls onto the table and glues himself to it. He cannot get up, and his teacher worries because school will end soon. Noah, Izzy, and Owen try to help by lassoing him, but the ropes snap. Luke and Grace bring a tow truck, but it explodes. The school nurse checks him and cannot send him home early. The principal leaves a note on Matty’s belly. Then Matty sees his teacher huffing and puffing and whispers a plan to Hailey and Owen. They use a huge paper fan, and the glue finally dries. When Matty’s dad arrives, he peels Matty off the table and calls him a masterpiece. At home, Dad opens the dried glue shape, fixes it, and hangs it on the fridge.

summary_text: The story asks what it would be like if people had animal teeth instead of their own. It first talks about beaver teeth, which are sharp like chisels, strong, and always growing. Then it describes great white shark teeth, which are long, sharp, and replaced by new teeth often. Next come narwhal teeth, where the left front tooth grows into a long tusk. Elephant tusks are described as strong front teeth used for digging and pulling roots. The story also explains rattlesnake fangs, which fold up and inject venom, and naked mole rat teeth, which help dig tunnels and pick up food. It continues with vampire bat teeth, hippopotamus teeth, bengal tiger teeth, crocodile teeth, and camel teeth. At the end, the story says animal teeth might be useful, but people do not need them for those jobs. Instead, the new teeth will be people teeth for biting, talking, and smiling.

summary_text: Martin Luther King Jr. was a boy who often got hurt, but he always got back up. He loved books even before he could read and said he wanted to get big words when he grew up. When he was 6, he had a white friend and they played together every day. Then they had to go to different schools, and his friend said they could not play anymore because his father said so. Martin learned this was because Martin was Black and his friend was white. His parents told him to choose love instead of hate and taught him that he was as good as anyone else. As he grew older, he saw unfair rules everywhere. Black people had worse schools and had to use different fountains, bathrooms, and lunch places. When he was 14, he was forced to give up his bus seat. Later, he studied religion and learned about nonviolent resistance from Henry David Thoreau and Mahatma Gandhi. He used peaceful protests, speeches, and marches to fight unfair treatment and help change the laws.

summary_text: Martin Luther King Jr. tells about his childhood, when he often got hurt but always got back up. Even before he could read, he loved books and wanted to learn “big words.” He also remembers playing with a white boy whose father owned a store across the street. They had fun together until they started school and were separated by race. The boy was no longer allowed to play with him, and Martin felt angry and confused. His parents explained that black people and white people were treated differently. They taught him to choose love instead of hate and to remember that he was as good as anyone else. As he grew up, Martin saw unfair treatment everywhere, including in schools, buses, and restaurants. Later, after studying nonviolence and the ideas of Gandhi, he helped lead peaceful protests, including the Montgomery bus boycott after Rosa Parks was arrested. These actions helped change unfair laws.

summary_text: Callie and her twin brother Charlie have always been together, even in Mommy’s tummy. They share curly hair, brown eyes, hot chocolate with marshmallows, their dog Harriett, music, football, and names that start with C. Callie is two minutes younger and loves to talk and watch the sky. Charlie is skinnier, goofier, and quieter. As babies, Callie showed love by talking, snuggling, and kissing Mommy, but Charlie did not. Mommy saw that Charlie was different and later learned that he has autism. This makes it harder for him to make friends, show feelings, and stay safe. Sometimes Charlie is hard to understand and can ruin playdates, but he also shows love in his own ways. He smiles, plays hand games, helps with Harriett, and runs to comfort Callie when she gets hurt. One day, after Callie hurt her toe, Charlie said, “Don’t cry, Callie, I love you.” Callie said it back, and she knows their love is shown in many ways.

summary_text: Snow can arrive in different ways. Sometimes it falls softly at night, like a shy friend waiting in the yard. This gentle snow brings peace. Other times, big cheerful flakes fall while people are at school or work, promising to send them home early over slippery white roads. Some snow is light enough to show tree branches, lamppost light, and a sparrow’s feet. Other snow is so heavy that it covers cars, bends evergreen trees, and keeps cats curled up indoors. Children love snow. They put on red boots and mittens, catch flakes on their tongues, and roll down hills. Snow gives them snow angels and new friends. While it stays, people can walk through the beautiful world, return to quiet homes, drink something warm, read, play, or talk together. The snow falls while flowers, the sun, and gardens sleep. It reminds everyone that moments do not last forever, but memories do.

That night, Squirrel worries, but the next morning many flowers have grown, and there are enough flowers for everyone.

summary_text: There was once a bear who was full of love and happiness. As he walked through the forest, he hugged every living thing he met. He hugged small rabbits, big animals, and even creatures that bears usually eat. Nothing was too big, too small, too smelly, or too scary for him to hug. But the bear loved trees most of all. He hugged big trees, little trees, apple trees, pear trees, and peach trees. One day, while he was hugging a beaver and a tree at the same time, he saw a man with an axe walk into the forest. The bear followed him to a very tall, old, beautiful tree. The man started to chop it down. The bear got very upset and almost bit the man, but he stopped because he could not eat him. Then the bear gave the man a big hug. The man dropped his axe and ran away, and the bear hugged the tree.

Then he meets Chester, a child ghost who just moved there with his grandma. Chester wants to be a ghost too, so Simon tells him how to look spooky and gives him a schedule. But Simon really wants Chester to do the chores while he goes off. Chester tries the tasks, but he is not very scary and gets confused. Later, Simon feels bad and helps Chester with human chores like vacuuming and laundry. In the end, Simon and Chester learn they are both better at being friends than at being ghosts or humans.

The tree wiggled, wobbled, shook, and stretched until it was awake. Then the Story Fairy went to the Albert Hall and held the storybook up high. When she opened it, the story was back inside. Everyone thanked the Story Tree for the best story ever.

summary_text: Spookley was a little pumpkin who grew in a pumpkin patch. The other pumpkins were round and could roll, but Spookley was square and could not move. They teased him, and he wished he could be round. Then a great storm came just before Halloween. The wind tossed the pumpkins around and broke the fence. Three pumpkins rolled toward the bay. Spookley tried and tried, then tipped onto his side and blocked the hole in the fence. He saved the other pumpkins, but many pumpkins crashed into him and piled on top of him. In the morning, the farmer found Spookley bruised but still strong. The farmer saved Spookley’s seeds and planted them everywhere. The next year, pumpkins grew in many shapes and colors. People came to choose round, triangular, and square pumpkins. Spookley’s story showed that a pumpkin should not be judged by its shape.

summary_text: Legend says tiny leprechauns visit once a year. On the night before St. Patrick’s Day, people try to catch one so he will grant a wish. To do this, they build a trap with a box, a bottle cap, glitter glue, tape, gold paint, rocks, and a rainbow slide. They close the drapes, dim the light, and wait quietly in the dark. Then they hear a sound and check the trap. But the leprechaun escapes. He leaves behind one shoe and a small note. The note says his name is Liam the Leprechaun and thanks the children for the shiny gold rocks and glitter, but says a cardboard box cannot trap him. The story ends by saying it is a shame he got away, but children should enjoy Saint Patrick’s Day and try again next year.

summary_text: One Thursday, a wonder fell from the sky into the garden. Ladybug saw it land on a leaf and said it bounced three times. Inchworm said it bounced only twice. The insects all thought it was amazing. Frog thought it was a gumdrop, but he did not like the taste. Dung beetle tried to roll it, but it was too heavy. Stink bug thought it may have grown from the ground. Grasshopper said it was not of Earthly Origins and guessed it was a fallen star, a comet, or a small planet. Luna Moth knew it was a magical Chrysalis and stayed with it through the night, but it did not hatch. In the morning, crafty Spider said it belonged to him because it had fallen into his web. He built Wonderville to show it off, charged tickets, and grew rich. Later, a five-legged creature stole the wonder and took it back to the sky. The insects returned to the garden, and Spider was left alone. Then Spider looked at the stars, spun high in the flowers, and more wonders fell from the sky.

April’s dad was still captured, so the turtles decided to rescue him together. Now they were truly a team.

summary_text: George’s mother wants George to bark like a dog. She asks him again and again, but George says no. She kisses the vet, the cat, the duck, the pig, and the cow. On the way home, she proudly asks George to bark for everyone. This time, George says, “Hello.”

summary_text: Tama worked in the library at Minidoka, a prison camp in the desert where many Japanese Americans were forced to live. She did not like the dust, the fences, or the guards, but she kept going to work because she loved books. Every day, George came to the library with the books he had borrowed, and Tama unlocked the door for him. Life in the camp was hard in every season, and Tama did not know when she would leave. She saw that the camp was full of sadness, fear, and unfairness, but the library gave her something steady to hold on to. She loved how books could hold many worlds inside them. One day, Tama felt overwhelmed and could not find the right word for how she felt. George told her the word was “human.” His kindness helped her feel less alone. Later, Tama and George married, had a son in Minidoka, and kept hoping for a better future.

summary_text: An egg rolled through the trees, across a meadow, and down a hill into Mother Duck’s nest. Four ducklings hatched. One had blue spots, one had brown stripes, one was yellow, and the fourth was an odd-looking duckling named GUI GUI. Mother Duck taught them to swim, dive, and waddle. GUI GUI learned quickly and grew big and strong, but Mother Duck loved all four ducklings equally. One day, three crocodiles came from the lake. They told GUI GUI that he was a crocodile and asked him to bring the ducks to the bridge. They planned to eat them. GUI GUI felt worried, but he made a plan. He brought the ducks to the bridge, but dropped three hard rocks instead. The crocodiles bit the rocks and broke their teeth. They ran away, and GUI GUI saved the ducks. Everyone celebrated, and GUI GUI lived happily with his duck family.

When they are done, Amy eats the perfect bow and even the imperfect ones. They all taste good.

summary_text: Parker Curry loved to dance in her tutu and dreamed of being a Dancing Queen. On a rainy Tuesday, she did not go to dance class. Instead, her mother took Parker, her sister Ava, and her best friend Gia to the museum. They put on boots and jackets and went inside, splashing and smiling. In the museum hall, the girls saw many paintings, including prancing horses, blooming flowers, a necklace, peacocks, fish, and many feathers. Then Gia ran to a playroom, and Parker followed her. The girls played with purple hair, a pirate hat, and sunglasses. When it was time to go home, Parker saw a row of frilly white tutus and began dancing after Gia. Then she stopped at a portrait of Michelle Obama. She looked at the painting and listened to her mother describe Michelle Obama as a mother, lawyer, writer, and hero. Parker felt strong and hopeful, and she shared the moment with Ava.

They make it through and go back home to Fruit Garden, where they rest in the sky under the sun.

summary_text: An old sao sent her three little pigs into the world. The first pig built a house from straw, and the second built a house from sticks. A hungry wolf came to each house. He huffed and puffed, blew each house down, and gobbled up each little pig. The third pig built a strong house from bricks. The wolf could not blow it down, so he tried tricks. The clever pig gathered turnips before the wolf arrived and picked apples before the wolf could catch him. At a fair, the pig hid inside a butter churn and rolled down the hill. The wolf became frightened and ran home. Later, the angry wolf climbed onto the brick house roof. The third pig made a fire under a big iron pot. When the wolf came down, the pig cooked and gobbled him up.

summary_text: Thousands of years ago, the first people came to America from Asia. By the time Columbus arrived, many Indian tribes lived across the land and spoke different languages. European settlers met these tribes, sometimes sharing knowledge and sometimes fighting over land. The story describes how different tribes lived. Algonquian people hunted and fished near the Atlantic and lived in wigwams. The Seminoles lived in Florida swamps, while the Iroquois lived in long houses. Plains tribes followed buffalo herds, using horses, hides, bones, and every part of the animals. Pueblo people built adobe homes and grew crops in dry places. Apache people hunted, and Navajo people raised sheep and made blankets. Northwest Coast tribes fished, hunted whales, carved totem poles, and held feasts. Indian languages gave names to many places. Plains tribes also used sign language and smoke signals to communicate.

summary_text: The first people in America were Indians, who came from Asia thousands of years ago. When Columbus arrived in 1492, he called the people Indians, although each tribe had its own name and language. European settlers moved west, sometimes sharing knowledge with tribes but often fighting them for land, until Indians lost most of their land. Different tribes adapted to their regions. Algonquian and Wampanoag people lived near the Atlantic and taught settlers to grow corn and squash. Seminoles escaped to Florida swamps, while Iroquois lived in long houses. Plains tribes followed buffalo, especially after horses arrived, using nearly every part of the animal for food, clothing, tools, and homes. Pueblo peoples farmed dry lands, built adobe homes, and held dances and meetings in kivas. Navajos raised sheep and wove blankets. Northwest Coast tribes fished, hunted whales, carved totem poles, and held potlatches. Tribes also used sign language and smoke signals to communicate across distances.

summary_text: In autumn, a strong wind carries many flower seeds across the land. The Tiny Seed is smaller and slower than the others. Some seeds are burned by the sun, frozen on a mountain, drowned in the ocean, or left in the hot desert. The Tiny Seed survives. A bird and a mouse do not see it, so it rests safely through winter. In spring, the seeds open and grow roots, stems, and leaves. A weed takes sunlight and rain from one little plant, and a child breaks another. The Tiny Seed finally grows, but flowers and plants around it are damaged or picked. The Tiny Plant keeps growing through summer. It becomes taller than people, trees, and houses. A giant flower grows, and birds, bees, and butterflies visit it. In autumn, the wind shakes the flower. Its seed pod opens, and many tiny seeds fly away.

summary_text: Ben Ripley is a twelve-year-old who thinks his life is ordinary. He goes to school, struggles with bullies, and secretly dreams of becoming a spy. One day, CIA agent Alexander Hale appears in Ben’s house and explains that the agency has been watching him. Ben is a brilliant student with unusual mathematical and testing abilities, so the CIA accepts him into its secret Academy of Espionage. Ben leaves home immediately, even though he must pretend to attend a normal science academy. At the school, Alexander suddenly tells him to run because armed attackers are shooting at them. Ben reaches a dormitory and is tackled by a mysterious girl named Erica. She gives him a taser and explains that enemies have taken students and teachers hostage. Erica escaped because she skipped the assembly where everyone else was captured. Ben learns that dozens of dangerous commandos are inside the school. Although he has only just arrived, he must help face the crisis.

summary_text: The Wolf was making a birthday cake for his dear old granny when he ran out of sugar. He walked to the first little pig’s house, which was made of straw. The Wolf knocked, but the house fell in. He called for the pig, then started to sneeze because of the straw. He huffed and snuffed, and a big sneeze made the straw house fall down. The first little pig was inside, and the Wolf ate the ham dinner left there. Next, the Wolf went to the second little pig’s house, which was made of sticks. He knocked and called, but no one answered. Then he sneezed again, and the stick house fell down too. The second little pig was inside, and the Wolf ate dinner again. After that, the Wolf went to the third little pig’s brick house and asked for sugar. The pig was rude, and the Wolf got angry. Police came, and the Wolf was taken to jail.

summary_text: A very thirsty crow looked everywhere for water. At last, she found a pitcher with some cool water inside. But the pitcher had a narrow neck, and the crow could not reach the water at the bottom. She tried, but she still could not drink. Then the crow stopped and thought. Soon she had an idea. She picked up small pebbles from the ground and dropped them into the pitcher, one by one. Each pebble made the water rise a little higher. The crow kept adding pebbles until the water came up close enough for her to drink. At last, she could reach the cool water and take a drink. After she was refreshed, the crow said, “Necessity is the mother of invention.”

At the end, everyone wiggles, even on the moon.

summary_text: Bruce was a bear who liked to be alone, so he often rode his bike to a stream to fish in peace. One morning, he tried to enjoy a quiet day, but a crowd was already there asking him to join a protest. Bruce went fishing anyway, but something kept taking his bait. He left, but the crowd had grown, and people thought he had come to save the forest. At town hall, Bruce and the others spoke about how a factory would hurt the forest and water. The town council said the land had been bought legally and the factory could be built unless there was a legal reason to stop it. Then Bruce’s empty lunchbox was found with two rare cobblestone tiger beetles in it. Since these beetles lived in the forest, the land had to be protected. The factory was stopped, and the forest became Bruce Wildland Park.

Daddy said everyone should go to sleep, and they did. After that, he read Mother Goose every night, and everyone got sleep.

summary_text: Liam lived in a city with no gardens, trees, or greenery, but he loved being outdoors. One day, he explored an old railway and found a small patch of wild flowers and plants. The plants were dying, so Liam came back every day to care for them. He learned how to water and prune them, and soon the little patch became a real garden. The garden began to grow along the railway. Weeds and mosses moved first, and then the more delicate plants followed. Liam explored the railway with the curious garden through spring, summer, and autumn. In winter, snow kept him away, so he prepared tools and plans for spring. When the snow melted, the sun and Liam’s help woke the plants. The garden spread into the city. Many years later, the whole city was filled with gardens, but Liam’s favorite garden was still the one where everything began.

summary_text: Luc lived in a small mountain village in Mexico with her mama, papa, and little brother and sister, Paco and Lupe. Papa worked in the fields with their burro, Papito, and Luc helped at home by feeding Papito, cleaning the casita, and caring for her siblings. Near Christmas, Padre Alvarez asked Luc’s mama to weave a new blanket for the baby Jesus in the Christmas procession. Luc and her mama bought wool, dyed it bright rainbow colors, and began weaving it on the loom. But then Luc’s mama became sick and had to go with Papa to the town doctor. Papa stayed with her, and Luc had to care for Paco and Lupe. She tried to finish the blanket, but the yarn became tangled and could not be fixed. On Christmas Eve, Luc went to the church with only weeds as a gift. The old woman told her that any gift given with love is beautiful. Luc placed the weeds by the manger, and they changed into shining red stars.

summary_text: Anne Frank was a Jewish girl who loved playing, watching movies, collecting autographs, and writing stories. She lived in Germany when Adolf Hitler and the Nazis began treating Jewish people cruelly. Anne’s family moved to Amsterdam, but the Nazis soon took over there too. Jewish people lost many freedoms, and Anne’s sister received a notice that meant she might be sent to a concentration camp. Anne’s family went into hiding in a secret space behind a bookcase. Seven people lived there quietly for more than two years. Helpful friends brought them food, books, and news. Anne studied, wrote in her diary, and found hope by looking at the sky and a chestnut tree. The people in hiding were eventually found, and Anne died during the Holocaust. Her diary was saved and became famous. Anne’s story reminds us to help people, speak up against unfairness, and look for hope even in dark times.

summary_text: Anne Frank was born in Germany and loved games, movies, writing, and her diary. Because Adolf Hitler and the Nazis persecuted Jewish people, her family moved to Amsterdam, but Germany invaded the Netherlands in 1940. New laws took away Jewish people's freedoms, and Anne's sister Margot received a call-up notice for a concentration camp. Soon after, Anne's family hid with the Van Pelses and Fritz Pfeffer in the Secret Annex, behind a bookcase in her father's office. They stayed there for two years and one month, living quietly, studying, and depending on helpers such as Miep, Johannes Kleiman, and Johan Voskuijl. Anne wrote to "Kitty," decorated her room, and found hope in the sky and a chestnut tree. The Nazis were defeated, but six million Jews, including Anne, were killed in the Holocaust. Miep gave Anne's diary to her father, and it became famous. Anne's story asks people to help others, oppose unfairness, and remember that people can be good at heart.

After being chased away, the minions built a new home, but they felt sad because they had no bad guy to serve. Then Kevin decided to leave and find a new master. Finally, the principal said Farmer Jake and the animals could be special guest visitors for Farm days. Turkey and his pals sang a farm song with the children, and everyone cheered.

The man with the yellow hat and the director put the puppies back. Then George opened another door and found the missing puppy. Everyone was happy, and the director gave the puppies and their mother a snack.

summary_text: Rosie Revere dreamed of being a great engineer. At Lila Greer’s classroom at Blue River Creek, she was shy and did not speak much. When no one was looking, she searched the trash for parts and built gadgets late at night in her attic hideaway. Long ago, Rosie had made inventions for her uncles and aunts, including a hotdog dispenser and helium pants. She made Zookeeper Fred a cheese hat to keep snakes away, but he laughed at it. Rosie felt embarrassed and hid her dreams. One autumn day, her great, great aunt Rose came to stay and talked about building airplanes. She wished she could fly. Rosie stayed awake and decided to make a machine for her aunt. She built the Cheese-copter and tested it outside. It flew for a moment, then crashed. Aunt Rose laughed, but then she hugged Rosie and said the first try was a success because it had flown. Rosie understood that quitting is the only real failure, and she kept dreaming and building.

Robins return, petals blossom, fish wake, streams run down the hills, dew rests on meadows, and birds come back. Winter ends, and spring arrives.

summary_text: On a winter night, snow drifts down from the sky, falling through sycamore branches and onto a husky’s bushy tail. Fish huddle beneath a frozen pond, while snowy dust blows across a cold glasshouse. Trees look like slender ghosts through its glass panels, and the last logs are covered with snow. Along the winterbrook, rocks and sticks freeze in the ice, and footprints disappear under falling snow. Trees shudder in a rising storm, while an empty nest holds its twigs together against the wind. By morning, orange hills glow in the early light. In sunlight, slush and snow soak into the cold ground; in shadow, they stay still and icy. Then winter thaws. New leaves, waking animals, bright sun, budding flowers, green grass, and robins appear. The pond shines blue, fish wake, streams run down hills, dew covers meadows, and birds return. Goodbye, winter. Hello, spring, you.

When her teacher announced a talent show, Penelope bravely signed up to rock and roll. She planned a colorful outfit, but during rehearsal she froze and could not sing or play. She began to think dinosaurs could not rock. Penelope stopped playing with friends and crossed her name off the list. Her father showed her family pictures and reminded her that being a T-Rex was only one part of who she was. Penelope was also kind, caring, creative, and adventurous. At school, her classmates asked to join her band. On show night, Penelope and the Mustard Seeds performed. They came in second place, and Penelope was happy. She learned that being yourself takes courage.

summary_text: Rey Montagu grew up in Arkansas and became interested in engineering when her grandfather took her to see a submarine. She wanted to design ships, but people laughed because she was a Black girl. Her mother told her to stay strong and use her brains. Schools were segregated, and Black students received fewer opportunities, but Rey studied hard and learned mathematics. When an engineering school would not admit Black students, she studied business instead. Later, she moved to Washington, D.C., and worked as a Navy clerk typist. Rey watched engineers, studied computers, and learned their work. When the staff became sick, she completed everyone’s work from memory and was promoted. When the Navy urgently needed ship plans, Rey created a computer system that finished the calculations in eighteen hours. Although she faced unfair treatment, she became the Navy’s first woman to lead ship design and achieved her dream.

summary_text: Rey Montague was born in Little Rock, Arkansas, in 1935. At seven, she toured a submarine, and learning that engineers had built it inspired her dream of engineering. Her mother warned that racism, sexism, and segregated schools might block her, but Rey studied hard, taught herself mathematics, and graduated with honors. When college refused to let a Black student study engineering, she earned a business degree instead. In Washington, D.C., Rey became a Navy clerk typist, learned ship-design work and computers, and was promoted after completing her own and the engineers’ work during an illness. Although her boss treated her poorly because of her race, she kept working. When the president ordered a ship quickly, Rey created a computer system that completed its blueprints in 18 hours and 26 minutes. The ship was built, but she was excluded from its launch. She later became the Navy’s first woman to lead ship design and earned honors as a professional engineer. Her story says to study hard, stay focused, and never quit.

Then Peter made his nest into a veranda with a straw roof. Paul made his nest into a fortress with a drawbridge, turrets, and cannons. Peter then built a hot tub, a home cinema, and a games room, with a ferris wheel, merry-go-round, and log flume outside. A storm came, and both big nests were too heavy. They fell apart and landed in a broken, soggy pile. An owl took Peter and Paul into her tree trunk home, gave them food and drink, and kept them dry. After that, Peter and Paul built a smaller home together in a hollow tree and welcomed other animals there when rain flooded their homes.

summary_text: One day, squirrels began skiing down the snowy hill near a quiet town. First there was one, then two, then many more, until 85 squirrels and more were gliding through town on little skis with poles. They skied over the town center, the village hall, and even near the church. The town people woke up and saw the squirrels everywhere. The squirrels had so much fun that they forgot to eat lunch. The mayor called a meeting because the town did not know how to stop them. Mr. Powers wanted to use traps and a vacuum device, but Sally Sue Breeze, a reporter, said the squirrels were getting thin and needed help. She followed their tracks to an old building where a rabbit was selling skis made from old popsicle sticks and poles made from toothpicks. Sally found the squirrel skis, the rabbits, and the nuts they had paid with. Then she helped bring the squirrels warm food, and later the town gave them a ski chalet where they could ski safely.

summary_text: Once upon a time, three little pigs lived with their kind mother. One day, Mama Pig told them it was time to leave home and build their own houses. She warned them about the big bad wolf. The first little pig met a man with straw and quickly built a straw house. The second little pig met a man with sticks and built a stick house. The third little pig met a man with bricks and carefully built a strong brick house. Then the big bad wolf came to the first house and said, “Little pig, little pig, let me in.” The pig refused, so the wolf huffed and puffed and blew the straw house down. The first pig ran to his brother’s stick house. The wolf blew that house down too. Both pigs ran to the brick house. The wolf tried to blow it down, but he could not. He tried the door and the chimney, but the third pig’s house stayed strong. In the end, the wolf was catapulted far away, and no one saw him again.

Toad was happy and said Frog was right, because growing a garden was hard work.

summary_text: A grape tells how he used to be sweet, kind, and thankful when he lived in a big bunch with his family. His grandparents taught the grapes to be kind, forgiving, considerate, and grateful, and to stay sweet no matter what happened. But one birthday changed him. He planned a big party with a fair, a magician, hay rides, snacks, and fireworks. He waited for everyone to come, but nobody arrived. After that, he became angry and started holding grudges against others. Later, he tried to meet his friend Lenny, but bad luck made him late. Lenny got upset and would not listen, and the grape saw how much their anger looked alike. On the way home, he found an old photo of himself and the wrong invitation date. He learned the party had been planned for the wrong day. After that, he began talking things out, letting go of grudges, and becoming sweet again.

summary_text: Tim carved his first pumpkin and named the Jack-o-Lantern Jack. He liked Jack very much and kept him for a while, but Mom said the pumpkin would rot and needed to go outside. Tim carried Jack to the garden and left him there. As the days passed, Jack changed. He got wrinkled, then moldy, and then flat. Winter snow covered him, and Tim forgot about him. Tim watered it and watched it grow into a pumpkin vine. Yellow flowers came and went, and then a small green pumpkin appeared. By Halloween, the pumpkins were orange, and Tim made one into a new Jack-o-Lantern and welcomed Jack back.

summary_text: Six truck friends go to a new job at a small airport. The traffic is slow, and everyone must wait. Hydrant dispenser fills fuel tanks, and tug pulls a plane for a check. More airplanes and trucks keep working while the airport grows. Cargo plane flies, and rubber removal machine cleans the runway. Crane truck, lift truck, and skid steer also help. Then snow starts to fall, and the runway gets covered. Snow plows, sweepers, blowers, and tankers clear the snow and ice. Icing truck sprays the planes so they can fly. When the big job is done, the airport crew waves goodbye, and the trucks roll off to sleep.

summary_text: A boy named Buzz had a pet fly named Fly Guy. Fly Guy could say, “Buzz.” One day, Dad asked, “Who wants to go for a ride?” Buzz and Fly Guy went with him. With the windows down, wind blew Fly Guy out of the car and into a truck. Buzz cried, “Follow that truck!” The truck driver spit Fly Guy into a motorboat. Buzz followed the boat, but Fly Guy jumped away when he saw a bug on a hook. He landed on a circus train. A sleepy elephant blew him onto an airplane. The pilot turned on the wipers, so Fly Guy flew away. Then a rocket roared up. Buzz and Dad followed it and landed the rocket. Buzz asked if Fly Guy was safe. Dad said the rocket did not take them to space. They rode home, and Fly Guy said, “More rides.”

summary_text: Mrs. Poodle had four puppies named Fifi, Fufu, la la, and Gaston. The puppies grew, and Gaston grew much bigger than the others. Mrs. Poodle taught them to sip, not slobber, to yep, not yap, and to walk with grace, not race. She also taught them to look pretty in pink, nibble their kibble, and ride in style. Gaston worked the hardest and practiced the longest. In spring, Mrs. Poodle took the puppies to the park. There she met Mrs. Bulldog and her puppies, Rocky, Ricky, Bruno, and Antoinette. The mothers saw that there had been a mix-up. Gaston and Antoinette traded places because each belonged with the other family. At first, the new puppies felt out of place. The next day, Mrs. Poodle and Mrs. Bulldog met again in the park, and Gaston and Antoinette traded back. After that, the two families played together every afternoon, and later Gaston and Antoinette had puppies of their own.

summary_text: Alice sat with her sister by a riverbank when a white rabbit hurried past, saying, “Oh dear! I shall be too late.” Alice followed it and fell down a rabbit hole. She landed in a hall with locked doors and a glass table with a key. After finding a tiny hidden door, she drank a bottle marked “drink me” and shrank so she could fit, but the key was too far away. Then she ate a cake marked “eat me” and grew very large. Alice cried, and her tears made a pool. The White Rabbit dropped gloves and a fan, and when Alice used the fan, she shrank again and fell into the Pool of Tears. There she met a duck, a Dodo, a Lori, an iglet, a mouse, and other creatures. They held a caucus race, and the Dodo said everyone had won. Alice gave out sweets, but the animals ran away, leaving her alone.

summary_text: Mortimer was lonely because he did not have a sweetheart before Cupid’s ball. He tried to win girls over in many ways. He gave a girl at the bus stop chocolates, the mail carrier a red heart, and a waitress a diamond ring. He read advice books, walked his dog, exercised at the gym, and took ballroom dancing lessons, but nothing helped. Then Mortimer placed a newspaper ad saying he was tall, dead, handsome, and wanted someone who liked graveyards, horror films, and Voodoo. On Saturday, he bought a new suit at the funeral home, fixed his hair, and went to Cupid’s ball. He waited by the punch bowl, but every girl ran away when he smiled. As the room emptied, Mortimer started to leave. Then he heard a crash and saw a beautiful girl named Mildred on the floor. She asked if she was too late, and Mortimer said she was right on time. They danced by moonlight and fell in love.

He gave a girl at the bus stop chocolates, gave the mail carrier a red heart, and gave a waitress a diamond ring with the finger still on it. He also read advice books, walked his dog, worked out, and took ballroom dancing lessons, but nothing helped. Then he placed a newspaper ad describing himself as tall, dead, and handsome. On Saturday he bought a suit at the funeral home, fixed his hair, and went to Cupid’s ball. He waited by the punch bowl, but every girl who came near screamed and ran away. Near midnight, the room emptied. Then a girl named Mildred fell to the floor. She was beautiful, and she asked if she was too late. Mortimer said she was right on time, and they danced by moonlight and fell in love.

summary_text: A long time ago, many people believed black people and white people should be kept apart. This was called segregation. Black children and white children could not always go to the same schools. The United States government said this was wrong and said children should be able to go to any school they wanted. Ruby Bridges was a little girl who first went to kindergarten at a school for black children. She liked her teacher and friends, but the William Franz Elementary School was closer to her home. The government said Ruby should be allowed to go there. In 1961, Ruby’s mother took her to the Franz school, and marshalls came to keep them safe. Some people stood outside and yelled at her, and many parents took their children home. Ruby stayed with her teacher, Mrs. Henry, and learned math and reading. After many months, other children came back, and Ruby finally had friends to play with. Later, many people read about Ruby, and artists and writers made her story famous. When Ruby grew up, she visited schools and told children to be kind to each other.

summary_text: Baby Monster is in a cave with Rabbit, Beaver, Squirrel, and Boore. The animals try to help her sleep. They read a story, sing a song, and count sheep. But Baby Monster wants to play. At the end, they find Baby Monster sleeping in a sunny place. Monster comes back and thanks the babysitters. The tired animals sit down, but their homes are still messy.

summary_text: In the morning, the big trucks were ready to work. Crane said, “Let’s hoist,” Dozer said, “Let’s push,” and Digger said, “Let’s dig, together.” They built tall buildings, roads, and bridges until the loud whistle blew. Then the trucks took a break, but Digger found a tiny flower in the rubble. He greeted it and cared for it every day. He watered it when it looked dry, shielded it on windy days, and sang it a bedtime song at night. The flower grew, but the city kept growing too. Soon there was only one empty space left. Crane said they needed to put a building there, and Dozer cut the flower down. When the smoke cleared, Digger saw little seeds in the rubble. He scooped them up and drove far away to a place no big truck had ever been. There he planted the seeds in warm earth and cared for them every day.

summary_text: Zayn loved adventures with his dad. After one very good day at the beach, Zayn asked what made it so perfect. His dad said they played at the beach and had “free fun,” but he would not say where it was. Zayn decided to find free fun the next day. He looked all through his house, then rode his bike around town and searched the pool, the park, and the playgrounds. He still could not find it, so he asked his dad to go hiking. They walked in the woods, explored caves, and climbed a peak, but Zayn was too busy searching to enjoy the trip. That night he said he could not find free fun. His dad told him to keep looking. The next morning Zayn remembered his dad’s words and went to the ocean. He rode a wave, fell into the water, and saw sea life all around him. Then he understood that free fun was everywhere when he slowed down and looked.

Howl confesses his love, they kiss, and together they defeat Madame Suliman and free Calcifer from the castle.

summary_text: Brother Bear and Sister Bear lived with Mama and Papa in a big treehouse. Brother was older and did not want to play tea party with Sister, so he went skateboarding with Freddy. Sister felt lonely, and Mama wished Sister had a cub friend her own age. Then a moving truck came to the empty treehouse down the road. It brought a new family with a little girl cub named Lizzy Bruin. Sister met Lizzy, and they played jump rope, where both girls bragged about how many jumps they could do. Then they went to the playground and had fun on the jungle gym, swings, seesaw, and grass. The next day Lizzy invited Sister to play school. They began to argue about who would be teacher, and they broke a pointer while wrestling for it. Sister went home angry and said she would never play with Lizzy again. Mama told her some games need two players, and Lizzy soon came back with Teddy, Sister’s forgotten toy. Sister thanked Lizzy, and they agreed to take turns being teacher and play together again.

All of Riley’s emotions work together each day, helping her life grow from a good day into a good week, year, and life.

summary_text: Detective dinosaur and Officer pterodactyl were on patrol one morning. Each time Detective dinosaur took a step, his shoe made a squeak. Officer pterodactyl asked if the shoe was too tight, too old, or needed polish, but Detective dinosaur said no each time. He said the shoe was squeaking because it was angry. Then he sang a song to the shoe, like his mother used to sing when he was little. While he sang, a mouse climbed out of the shoe and said he had been trying to nap, but Detective dinosaur’s big foot kept squeezing him. Detective dinosaur let the mouse go. After that, he put on the shoe and took a step. The shoe did not squeak anymore. Detective dinosaur said his shoe was no longer angry, and Officer pterodactyl flew away while Detective dinosaur walked on quietly.
